children.text: Chapter 1
vratamupaiṣyan
children.translated_text: When he is about to undertake the vow,

children.text: antareṇāhavanīyaṃ ca gārhapatyaṃ ca prāṅ tiṣṭhann apa upaspṛśati tadyadapa upaspṛśatyamedhyo vai puruṣo yadanṛtaṃ vadati tena pūtirantarato medhyā vā āpo medhyo bhūtvā vratamupāyānīti pavitraṃ vā āpaḥ pavitrapūto vratamupāyānīti tasmādvā apa upaspṛśati ||
children.translated_text: standing facing east between the <s>āhavanīya</s> and the <s>gārhapatya</s> fires, he touches water. In that he touches water: a man is impure when he speaks untruth; by that he becomes foul within. But waters are pure. Thinking, 'Having become pure, may I undertake the vow,' he touches water. Waters are a purifier; thinking, 'Purified by the purifier, may I undertake the vow,' therefore he touches water.

children.text: so 'gnim evābhīkṣamāṇo vratamupaiti
children.translated_text: Then, gazing directly at the fire, he undertakes the vow:

children.text: agne vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmi tacchakeyaṃ tanme rādhyatām ity agnir vai devānāṃ vratapatistasmā evaitatprāha vrataṃ cariṣyāmi tacchakeyaṃ tanme rādhyatāmiti nātra tirohitamivāsti ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Agni</s>, lord of vows, I shall observe the vow; may I be able to do it; may it succeed for me.' For <s>Agni</s> is the lord of vows among the gods. Therefore he says this to him: 'I shall observe the vow; may I be able to do it; may it succeed for me.' There is nothing hidden here, as it were.

children.text: atha saṃsthite visṛjate
children.translated_text: Then, when it has been completed, he releases it:

children.text: agne vratapate vratamacāriṣaṃ tad aśakam tanme 'rādhīty aśakaddhyetad yo yajñasya saṃsthām agann arādhi hyasmai yo yajñasya saṃsthām agannetena nveva bhūyiṣṭhā iva vratamupayanty anena tvevopeyāt ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Agni</s>, lord of vows, I have observed the vow; I was able to do it; it has succeeded for me.' For one who has reached the completion of the sacrifice has indeed been able to do this, and it has succeeded for one who has reached the completion of the sacrifice. Now by this formula most people undertake the vow, as it were; but he should undertake it by this one alone.

children.text: dvayaṃ vā idaṃ na tṛtīyamasti
children.translated_text: There are two things here, and there is no third:

children.text: satyaṃ caivānṛtaṃ ca satyameva devā anṛtam manuṣyā idamahamanṛtātsatyamupaimīti tanmanuṣyebhyo devānupaiti ||
children.translated_text: truth and untruth. Truth is the gods, untruth is men. Saying, 'From untruth I go to truth,' he thereby goes from men to the gods.

children.text: sa vai satyameva vadet
children.translated_text: He should indeed speak only truth.

children.text: etaddhavai devā vrataṃ caranti yatsatyaṃ tasmātte yaśo yaśo ha bhavati ya evaṃ vidvāṃt satyaṃ vadati ||
children.translated_text: For this, namely truth, is the vow that the gods observe. Therefore they have glory; and glory belongs to the one who, knowing thus, speaks truth.

children.text: atha saṃsthite visṛjate
children.translated_text: Then, when it has been completed, he releases it:

children.text: idamahaṃ ya evāsmi so 'smīty amānuṣa iva vā etadbhavati yadvratamupaiti na hi tadavakalpate yadbrūyād idamahaṃ satyādanṛtamupaimīti tad u khalu punarmānuṣo bhavati tasmādidam ahaṃ ya evāsmi so 'smītyevaṃ vrataṃ visṛjeta ||
children.translated_text: 'I am this, just the one that I am.' For when he undertakes the vow, he becomes, as it were, non-human. It would not be fitting for him to say, 'From truth I go to untruth.' But then he becomes human again. Therefore he should release the vow in this way: 'I am this, just the one that I am.'

children.text: athāto 'śanānaśanasyaiva
children.translated_text: Now, then, concerning eating and not eating.

children.text: tad u hāṣāḍhaḥ sāvayaso 'naśanameva vratam mene mano ha vai devā manuṣyasyājānanti ta enametadvratamupayantaṃ viduḥ prātarno yakṣyata iti te 'sya viśve devā gṛhān āgacchanti te 'sya gṛheṣūpavasanti sa upavasathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On this matter <s>Āṣāḍha Sāvayasa</s> held that fasting alone was the vow. For the gods know a man's mind. They know him as he undertakes this vow: 'Tomorrow he will sacrifice for us.' All the gods come to his house; they dwell fasting in his houses. That is the <s>upavasatha</s> (fast-day dwelling).

children.text: tannvevānavakﾱptam
children.translated_text: But that is certainly not properly established.

children.text: yo manuṣyeṣv anaśnatsu pūrvo 'śnīyād atha kimu yo deveṣv anaśnatsu pūrvo 'śnīyāt tasmād u naivāśnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: If one among men who are not eating were to eat first, how much more so if one among gods who are not eating were to eat first? Therefore he should not eat at all.

children.text: tad u hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ
children.translated_text: On this matter <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:

children.text: yadi nāśnāti pitṛdevatyo bhavati yady u aśnāti devānatyaśnātīti sa yadevāśitam anaśitaṃ tadaśnīyāditi yasya vai havirna gṛhṇanti tadaśitam anaśitaṃ sa yadaśnāti tenāpitṛdevatyo bhavati yady u tadaśnāti yasya havirna gṛhṇanti teno devānnātyaśnāti ||
children.translated_text: 'If he does not eat, he becomes one whose deities are the Fathers; but if he eats, he has eaten before the gods. Therefore he should eat what is both eaten and uneaten.' For when they do not take a person's oblation, that is eaten and uneaten. When he eats that, he does not thereby become one whose deities are the Fathers; and if he eats that whose oblation they do not take, he thereby does not eat before the gods.

children.text: sa vā āraṇyamevāśnīyāt
children.translated_text: He should therefore eat only forest food.

children.text: yā vāraṇyā oṣadhayo yadvā vṛkṣyaṃ tad u ha smāhāpi barkurvārṣṇo māsānme pacata na vā eteṣāṃ havirgṛhṇantīti tad u tathā na kuryād vrīhiyavayorvā etadupajaṃ yacchamīdhānyaṃ tadvrīhiyavāvevaitena bhūyāṃsau karoti tasmādāraṇyamevāśnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: Whatever plants are of the forest, or whatever belongs to trees. On this matter <s>Barku Vārṣṇa</s> used to say, 'Cook beans for me, for they do not take an oblation of these.' But he should not do that. For what is called pulse-grain is a growth of rice and barley; by that he merely makes rice and barley more abundant. Therefore he should eat only forest food.

children.text: sa āhavanīyāgāre vaitāṃ rātrīṃ śayīta
children.translated_text: He should sleep that night in the house of the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire,

children.text: gārhapatyāgāre vā devānvā eṣa upāvartate yo vratamupaiti sa yānevopāvartate teṣāmevaitanmadhye śete 'dhaḥ śayītādhastādiva hi śreyasa upacāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: or in the house of the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire. For the one who undertakes the vow turns toward the gods. Among those toward whom he turns, he sleeps in their very midst. He should sleep below, for service to a superior is, as it were, from below.

children.text: sa vai prātar apa eva
children.translated_text: In the morning, he first approaches the waters alone

children.text: prathamena karmaṇābhipadyate 'paḥ praṇayati yajño vā āpo yajñamevaitatprathamena karmaṇābhipadyate tāḥ praṇayati yajñamevaitadvitanoti ||
children.translated_text: as the first act: he carries the waters forward. The waters are the sacrifice; therefore by the first act he approaches the sacrifice itself. He carries them forward; thereby he extends the sacrifice.

children.text: sa praṇayati
children.translated_text: He carries them forward, saying:

children.text: kastvā yunakti sa tvā yunakti kasmai tvā yunakti tasmai tvā yunaktīty etābhiraniruktābhir vyāhṛtibhir anirukto vai prajāpatiḥ prajāpatiryajñas tat prajāpatimevaitadyajñaṃ yunakti ||
children.translated_text: 'Who yokes you? He yokes you. For whom does he yoke you? For him he yokes you.' With these undefined utterances he does so; for <s>Prajāpati</s> is undefined, and <s>Prajāpati</s> is the sacrifice. Thus he yokes <s>Prajāpati</s>, the sacrifice itself.

children.text: yad v evāpaḥ praṇayati
children.translated_text: And further, in that he carries the waters forward:

children.text: adbhirvā idaṃ sarvamāptaṃ tatprathamenaivaitatkarmaṇā sarvamāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: by waters all this has been obtained. Thus by this very first act he obtains everything.

children.text: yadvevāsyātra
children.translated_text: And further, whatever here of his

children.text: hotā vādhvaryurvā brahmā vāgnīdhro vā svayaṃ vā yajamāno nābhyāpayati tadevāsyaitena sarvam āptam bhavati ||
children.translated_text: the <s>hotṛ</s>, or the <s>adhvaryu</s>, or the <s>brahman</s>, or the <s>agnīdh</s>, or the sacrificer himself does not fully obtain, all that becomes obtained for him by this act.

children.text: yadvevāpaḥ praṇayati
children.translated_text: And further, in that he carries the waters forward:

children.text: devānha vai yajñena yajamānāṃstān asurarakṣasāni rarakṣur na yakṣyadhva iti tadyadarakṣaṃstasmādrakṣāṃsi ||
children.translated_text: when the gods were sacrificing with the sacrifice, the <s>asuras</s> and <s>rakṣases</s> obstructed them, saying, 'You shall not sacrifice.' Because they obstructed, therefore they are called <s>rakṣāṃsi</s>.

children.text: tato devā etaṃ vajraṃ dadṛśuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the gods saw this <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt weapon):

children.text: yad apo vajro vā āpo vajro hi vā āpas tasmādyenaitā yanti nimnaṃ kurvanti yatropatiṣṭhante nirdahanti tata etaṃ vajram udayacchaṃs tasyābhaye 'nāṣṭre nivāte yajñamatanvata tatho evaiṣa etaṃ vajram udyacchati tasyābhaye 'nāṣṭre nivāte yajñaṃ tanute tasmādapaḥ praṇayati ||
children.translated_text: namely the waters. The waters are a <s>vajra</s>; indeed the waters are a <s>vajra</s>. Therefore, wherever they go, they make a hollow, and where they settle, they burn away. Then, raising this <s>vajra</s>, they spread out the sacrifice in its fearlessness, without injury, and sheltered from wind. So too this man raises this <s>vajra</s> and spreads out the sacrifice in its fearlessness, without injury, and sheltered from wind. Therefore he carries the waters forward.

children.text: tā utsicyottareṇa gārhapatyaṃ sādayati
children.translated_text: Having poured them out, he sets them down to the north of the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire.

children.text: yoṣā vā āpo vṛṣāgnir gṛhā vai gārhapatyas tad gṛheṣvevaitan mithunam prajananaṃ kriyate vajraṃ vā eṣa udyacchati yo 'paḥ praṇayati yo vā apratiṣṭhito vajram udyacchati nainaṃ śaknotyudyantuṃ saṃ hainaṃ śṛṇāti ||
children.translated_text: The waters are female, and fire is male; the gārhapatya fire is the household. Thus in the household this pair, this procreative union, is made. He who leads the waters forward raises a thunderbolt; and one who, not firmly established, raises a thunderbolt cannot lift it up: it smashes him.

children.text: sa yadgārhapatye sādayati
children.translated_text: So, when he sets them down on the gārhapatya fire,

children.text: gṛhā vai gārhapatyo gṛhā vai pratiṣṭhā tad gṛheṣvevaitat pratiṣṭhāyām pratitiṣṭhati tatho hainameṣa vajro na hinasti tasmādgārhapatye sādayati ||
children.translated_text: the gārhapatya is the household, and the household is firm support. Thus he stands firm in the household, in firm support. Therefore this thunderbolt does not injure him. For that reason he sets them down on the gārhapatya fire.

children.text: tā uttareṇāhavanīyam praṇayati
children.translated_text: He leads them to the north of the āhavanīya fire.

children.text: yoṣā vā āpo vṛṣāgnir mithunam evaitat prajananaṃ kriyata evamiva hi mithunaṃ kﾱptam uttarato hi strī pumāṃsamupaśete ||
children.translated_text: The waters are female and fire is male. Thus this pair, this procreative union, is made. For a pair is arranged in just this way: the woman lies down on the north side of the man.

children.text: tā nāntareṇa saṃcareyuḥ
children.translated_text: They should not pass between them.

children.text: nen mithunaṃ caryamāṇamantareṇa saṃcarāṇīti tā nātihṛtya sādayen no anāptāḥ sādayet sa yadatihṛtya sādayed asti vā agneścāpāṃ ca vibhrātṛvyamiva sa yatheva ha tadagnerbhavati yatrāsyāpa upaspṛśantyagnau hādhi bhrātṛvyaṃ vardhayed yadatihṛtya sādayed yad yo 'nāptāḥ sādayen no hābhistaṃ kāmam abhyāpayed yasmai kāmāya praṇīyante tasmād u sampratyevottareṇāhavanīyam praṇayati ||
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'May they not pass between the pair while it is being performed,' he should not set them down after carrying them too far, nor should he set them down before they have reached the place. If he were to set them down after carrying them too far, there is indeed a rivalry between fire and the waters; wherever his waters touch the fire, that much would belong to fire, and he would increase a rival in the fire. If he were to set them down before they had reached the place, he would not attain with them the desire for which they are led forward. Therefore he leads them forward exactly to the north of the āhavanīya.

children.text: atha tṛṇaiḥ paristṛṇāti
children.translated_text: Then he strews it around with grasses.

children.text: dvandvam pātrāṇyudāharati śūrpaṃ cāgnihotrahavaṇīṃ ca sphyaṃ ca kapālāni ca śamyāṃ ca kṛṣṇājinaṃ colūkhalamusale dṛṣadupale taddaśa daśākṣarā vai virāḍ virāḍvai yajñas tadvirājamevaitad yajñam abhisaṃpādayaty atha yaddvandvaṃ dvandvaṃ vai vīryaṃ yadā vai dvau saṃrabhete atha tadvīryam bhavati dvandvaṃ vai mithunam prajananam mithunamevaitatprajananaṃ kriyate ||
children.translated_text: He brings out the vessels in pairs: the winnowing basket and the agnihotra ladle, the wooden sword and the potsherds, the pin and the black antelope skin, the mortar and pestle, and the lower and upper grinding stones. That makes ten. The <s>virāj</s> has ten syllables; the sacrifice is the <s>virāj</s>. Thus he brings this sacrifice into conformity with the <s>virāj</s>. And because each is paired: pairedness is strength, for when two strive together, then strength arises. Pairedness is also a pair, procreation; thus this pair, this procreative union, is made.

children.text: Chapter 2
atha śūrpaṃ cāgnihotrahavaṇīṃ cādatte
children.translated_text: Then he takes the winnowing basket and the agnihotra ladle.

children.text: karmaṇe vāṃ veṣāya vāmiti yajño vai karma yajñāya hi tasmādāha karmaṇe vāmiti veṣāya vāmiti veveṣṭīva hi yajñam ||
children.translated_text: He says, 'For work I take you, for adornment I take you.' The sacrifice is work, for it is for the sacrifice; therefore he says, 'For work I take you.' He says, 'For adornment I take you,' for he as it were adorns the sacrifice.

children.text: atha vācaṃ yacchati
children.translated_text: Then he restrains his speech.

children.text: vāgvai yajño 'vikṣubdho yajñaṃ tanavā ity atha pratapati pratyuṣṭaṃ rakṣaḥ pratyuṣṭā arātayo niṣṭaptaṃ rakṣo niṣṭaptā arātaya iti vā ||
children.translated_text: Speech is the sacrifice. Thinking, 'May I extend the sacrifice undisturbed,' he then warms them, saying, 'The hostile spirit has been scorched; the enemies have been scorched. The hostile spirit has been thoroughly burned; the enemies have been thoroughly burned.'

children.text: devā ha vai yajñaṃ tanvānāḥ
children.translated_text: When the gods were extending the sacrifice,

children.text: te 'surarakṣasebhya āsaṅgād bibhayāṃcakrus tadyajñamukhād evaitannāṣṭrā rakṣāṃsyato 'pahanti ||
children.translated_text: they were afraid of attachment from the Asuras and <s>rakṣases</s>. Therefore, from the very mouth of the sacrifice, he drives away from here the hostile <s>rakṣases</s>.

children.text: atha praiti
children.translated_text: Then he goes forward.

children.text: urvantarikṣamanvemīty antarikṣaṃ vā anu rakṣaścaratyamūlamubhayataḥ paricchinnaṃ yathāyam puruṣo 'mūla ubhayataḥ paricchinno 'ntarikṣamanucarati tadbrahmaṇaivaitad antarikṣam abhayam anāṣṭraṃ kurute ||
children.translated_text: He says, 'I go along through the wide midspace.' A <s>rakṣas</s> moves along through the midspace, rootless and cut off on both sides, just as this man, rootless and cut off on both sides, moves along through the midspace. Thus by means of the sacred formulation he makes the midspace free from danger and free from hostile beings.

children.text: sa vā anasa eva gṛhṇīyāt
children.translated_text: He should take it from the cart itself.

children.text: ano ha vā agre paśceva vā idaṃ yacchālaṃ sa yadevāgre tat karavāṇīti tasmādanasa eva gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: In the beginning, the cart was indeed like the rear of this shed. Thinking, 'I shall do what was in the beginning,' he should therefore take it from the cart itself.

children.text: bhūmā vā anaḥ
children.translated_text: The cart is abundance.

children.text: bhūmā hi vā anas tasmādyadā bahu bhavaty anovāhyam abhūd ityāhus tad bhūmānam evaitad upaiti tasmādanasa eva gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: For the cart is indeed abundance. Therefore, when there is much, people say, 'It has become cart-loadable.' Thus he attains abundance. Therefore he should take it from the cart itself.

children.text: yajño vā anaḥ yajño hi vā anas tasmād anasa eva yajūṃṣi santi na kauṣṭhasya na kumbhyai bhastrāyai ha smarṣayo gṛhṇanti tad v ṛṣīn prati bhastrāyai yajūṃṣyāsus tānyetarhi prākṛtāni yajñādyajñaṃ nirmimā iti tasmādanasa eva gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: The cart is the sacrifice, for the cart is indeed the sacrifice. Therefore the sacrificial formulas belong to the cart itself, not to a box, not to a pot, nor to a leather bag. The seers, it is remembered, used to take from a leather bag; the sacrificial formulas for the leather bag belonged to those seers, but these are now ordinary ones: 'From sacrifice fashion sacrifice.' Therefore he should take it from the cart itself.

children.text: uto pātryai gṛhṇanti
children.translated_text: Yet they also take it from a vessel.

children.text: anantarāyam u tarhi yajūṃṣi japet sphyam u tarhy avastad upohya gṛhṇīyād yato yunajāma tato vimuñcāmeti yato hyeva yuñjanti tato vimuñcanti ||
children.translated_text: In that case he should mutter the sacrificial formulas without interruption. Then, having placed the wooden sword beneath it, he should take it, saying, 'From where we yoke, from there we unyoke'; for from the very place where they yoke, from there they unyoke.

children.text: tasya vā etasyānasaḥ
children.translated_text: Now of this cart,

children.text: agnireva dhūr agnirhi vai dhūr atha ya enadvahantyagnidagdhamivaiṣāṃ vaham bhavaty atha yajjaghanena kastambhīm praugaṃ vedirevāsya sā nīḍa eva havirdhānam ||
children.translated_text: fire itself is the pole, for fire is indeed the pole. And those who draw it have as it were a load burned by fire. What is behind, at the crossbar, is the pole-front; that is its altar. The nest is the havirdhāna, the oblation-shed.

children.text: sa dhuramabhimṛśati
children.translated_text: He touches the pole.

children.text: dhūrasi dhūrva dhūrvantaṃ dhūrva taṃ yo 'smān dhūrvati taṃ dhūrva yaṃ vayaṃ dhūrvāma ity agnirvā eṣa dhuryas tametadatyeṣyan bhavati havir grahīṣyaṃs tasmā evaitān nihnute tatho haitameṣo 'tiyantamagnirdhuryo na hinasti ||
children.translated_text: He says, 'You are the pole. Shake off the shaker; shake off him who shakes us; shake off him whom we shake.' This fire is the draught-bearer. When he is about to pass beyond it, intending to take the oblation, he makes these submissions to it. Thus this fire, the draught-bearer, does not injure him as he passes beyond.

children.text: taddha smaitadāruṇirāha
children.translated_text: Concerning this, <s>Āruṇi</s> used to say:

children.text: adharmāsaśo vā ahaṃ sapatnān dhūrvāmītyetaddha sma sa tadabhyāha ||
children.translated_text: 'Without violation of <s>dharma</s>, I shake off my rivals.' This indeed is what he used to add to it.

children.text: atha jaghanena kastambhīmīṣāmabhimṛśya japati
children.translated_text: Then, after touching the shaft behind the crossbar, he mutters:

children.text: devānāmasi vahnitamaṃ sasnitamam papritamaṃ juṣṭatamaṃ devahūtamam
children.translated_text: 'You are the best carrier of the gods, the best gainer, the best filler, the most pleasing, the best caller of the gods.'

children.text: ahrutamasi havirdhānaṃ dṛṃhasva mā hvārityana evaitad upastautyupastutād rātamanaso havirgṛhṇānīti mā te yajñapatir hvārṣīd iti yajamāno vai yajñapatis tad yajamānāyaivaitad uhvalāmāśāste ||
children.translated_text: 'You are uninjured; havirdhāna, be firm; do not swerve.' In this way he praises the cart. From the praised cart he takes the oblation with a gladdened mind. 'May your lord of the sacrifice not swerve.' The sacrificer is the lord of the sacrifice; thus for the sacrificer he hopes for freedom from swerving.

children.text: athākramate
children.translated_text: Then he steps up.

children.text: viṣṇustvā kramatāmiti yajño vai viṣṇuḥ sa devebhya imāṃ vikrāntiṃ vicakrame yaiṣāmiyaṃ vikrāntiridameva prathamena padena paspārāthedam antarikṣaṃ dvitīyena divamuttamenaitām vevaiṣa etasmai viṣṇuryajño vikrāntiṃ vikramate ||
children.translated_text: "May <s>Viṣṇu</s> stride for you." The sacrifice indeed is <s>Viṣṇu</s>. For the gods he strode out this stride, of which this is the stride: with the first step he touched this world, then the atmosphere with the second, and heaven with the highest. Thus <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the sacrifice, strides out this very stride for him.

children.text: atha prekṣate
children.translated_text: Then he looks forward.

children.text: uru vātāyeti prāṇo vai vātas tad brahmaṇaivaitat prāṇāya vātāyorugāyaṃ kurute ||
children.translated_text: "Wide for the wind." The wind is the breath; by this, through the brahman, he makes wide room for the breath, for the wind.

children.text: athāpāsyati
children.translated_text: Then he wipes it away.

children.text: apahataṃ rakṣa iti yadyatra kiṃcid āpannam bhavati yady u nābhy eva mṛśet tan nāṣṭrā evaitadrakṣāṃ syato 'pahanti ||
children.translated_text: "The rakṣas is smitten away." If anything has happened there, or even if he merely touches it, by this he strikes away the hostile rakṣases from there.

children.text: athābhipadyate
children.translated_text: Then he steps upon it.

children.text: yacantām pañcati pañca vā imā aṅgulayaḥ pāṅkto vai yajñastadyajñamevaitadatra dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: "Let the five yield." These five fingers are five; the sacrifice is fivefold. Thus he places the sacrifice itself here.

children.text: atha gṛhṇāti
children.translated_text: Then he takes hold of it.

children.text: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinorbāhubhyām pūṣṇo hastābhyām agnaye juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti savitā vai devānām prasavitā tat savitṛprasūta evaitadgṛhṇātyaśvinorbāhubhyāmityaśvināvadhvaryū pūṣṇo hastābhyāmiti pūṣā bhāgadugho 'śanam pāṇibhyāmupanidhātā satyaṃ devā antaṃ manuṣyāstat satyenaivaitad gṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: "At the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I take you, pleasing to <s>Agni</s>." <s>Savitṛ</s> is the impeller of the gods; therefore, impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, he takes it. "With the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>": the <s>Aśvins</s> are the two adhvaryus. "With the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>": <s>Pūṣan</s> is the allotter of shares, the provider who places food near with his hands. The gods are truth, men are the end; thus he takes it by truth itself.

children.text: atha devatāyā ādiśati
children.translated_text: Then he assigns it to the deity.

children.text: sarvā ha vai devatā adhvaryuṃ havir gṛhīṣyantam upatiṣṭhante mama nāma grahīṣyati mama nāma grahīṣyatīti tābhya evaitatsaha satībhyo 'samadaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: All the deities indeed attend upon the adhvaryu when he is about to take the oblation, thinking, "He will take my name, he will take my name." Thus, for those deities who are present together, he makes it without discord.

children.text: yad v eva devatāyā ādiśati
children.translated_text: And as to why he assigns it to the deity:

children.text: yāvatībhyo ha vai devatābhyo havīṃṣi gṛhyanta ṝṇamu haiva tāstena manyante yadasmai taṃ kāmaṃ samardhayeyur yat kāmyā gṛhṇāti tasmādvai devatāyā ādiśatyevam eva yathāpūrvaṃ havīṃṣi gṛhītvā ||
children.translated_text: For whatever deities the oblations are taken, they consider themselves under an obligation by that, so that they may fulfil for him the desire for which he takes the desired offering. Therefore he assigns it to the deity, precisely after taking the oblations in their proper order.

children.text: athābhimṛśati
children.translated_text: Then he touches it.

children.text: bhūtāya tvā nārātaya iti tadyata eva gṛhṇāti tadevaitatpunarāpyāyayati ||
children.translated_text: "For being I take you, not for enemies." Thus, from the very place from which he takes it, he replenishes it again.

children.text: atha prāṅprekṣate
children.translated_text: Then he looks eastward.

children.text: svar abhivikhyeṣam iti parivṛtamiva vā etadano bhavati tadasyaitaccakṣuḥ pāpmagṛhītamiva bhavati yajño vai svarahardevāḥ sūryas tat svar evaitad ato 'bhivipaśyati ||
children.translated_text: "May I look upon the heavenly light." This cart is, as it were, enclosed, and its eye is, as it were, seized by evil. The sacrifice is the heavenly light; the day is the gods; the sun is that heavenly light. Thus from here he looks upon that heavenly light.

children.text: athāvarohati
children.translated_text: Then he descends.

children.text: dṛṃhantāṃ duryāḥ pṛthivyāmiti gṛhā vai duryāste heta īśvaro gṛhā yajamānasya yo 'syaiṣo 'dhvaryuryajñena carati tam prayantamanu pracyotostasyeśvaraḥ kulaṃ vikṣobdhos tān evaitad asyām pṛthivyāṃ dṛṃhati tathā nānupracyavante tathā na vikṣobhante tasmādāha dṛṃhantāṃ duryāḥ pṛthivyāmityatha praityurvantarikṣamanvemīti so 'sāveva bandhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Let the doors be made firm upon the earth." The doors are the houses. For the houses of the sacrificer, whose adhvaryu here moves with the sacrifice, are liable to slip away after him as he goes, and his family is liable to be disturbed. Therefore he makes them firm upon this earth; in that way they do not slip after him, and in that way they are not disturbed. Therefore he says, "Let the doors be made firm upon the earth." Then he goes forth, saying, "I follow the wide atmosphere." That same connection applies there.

children.text: sa yasya gārhapatye havīṃṣi śrapayanti
children.translated_text: Now, for the man whose oblations they cook on the gārhapatya fire:

children.text: gārhapatye tasya pātrāṇi saṃsādayanti jaghaneno tarhi gārhapatyaṃ sādayedyasyāhavanīye havīṃṣi śrapayantyāhavanīye tasya pātrāṇi saṃsādayanti jaghaneno tarhyāhavanīyaṃ sādayetpṛthivyāstvā nābhau sādayāmīti madhyaṃ vai nābhirmadhyamabhayaṃ tasmādāha pṛthivyāstvā nābhau sādayāmītyadityā upastha ityupastha ivainadabhārṣuriti vā āhur yat suguptaṃ gopāyanti tasmādāhādityā upastha ityagne havyaṃ rakṣeti tadagnaye caivaitaddhaviḥ paridadāti guptyā asyai ca pṛthivyai tasmādāhāgne havyaṃ rakṣeti ||
children.translated_text: they set down his vessels at the gārhapatya. In that case he should set them down behind the gārhapatya. For the man whose oblations they cook on the āhavanīya fire, they set down his vessels at the āhavanīya; in that case he should set them down behind the āhavanīya. "I set you down in the navel of the earth." The navel is the middle, and the middle is security; therefore he says, "I set you down in the navel of the earth." "In the lap of <s>Aditi</s>." When people guard what is well protected, they say, "They have borne it as in a lap"; therefore he says, "In the lap of <s>Aditi</s>." "<s>Agni</s>, protect the oblation." Thus he entrusts this oblation both to <s>Agni</s>, for protection, and to this earth; therefore he says, "<s>Agni</s>, protect the oblation."

children.text: Chapter 3
sa vai kapālānyevānyatara upadadhāti
children.translated_text: Now one of them lays down the potsherds.

children.text: dṛṣadupale anyatarastadvā etadubhayaṃ saha kriyate tadyadetadubhayaṃ saha kriyate ||
children.translated_text: The other lays down the grinding stone and muller. This twofold act is done together; and as to why this twofold act is done together:

children.text: śiro ha vā etadyajñasya yatpuroḍāśaḥ sa gānyevemāni śīrṣṇaḥ kapālānyetānyevāsya kapālāni mastiSka eva piṣṭāni tadvā etadekamaṅgamekaṃ saha karavāva samānaṃ karavāveti tasmādvā etadubhayaṃ saha kriyate ||
children.translated_text: The puroḍāśa is indeed the head of the sacrifice. These are the bones of the head, namely the potsherds; these are its skull bones, and the ground grains are the brain. Therefore this is one limb, one thing; "let us do it together, let us make it the same." Therefore this twofold act is done together.

children.text: sa yaḥ kapālānyupadadhāti
children.translated_text: The one who lays down the potsherds

children.text: sa upaveṣamādatte dhṛṣṭirasīti sa yadenenāgniṃ dhṛṣṇivopacarati tena dhṛSṭiratha yadenena yajña upālabhata upeva vā enenaitadveṣṭi tasmādupaveṣo nāma ||
children.translated_text: takes the poker, saying, "You are bold." Because with it he approaches the fire boldly, by that it is called bold; and because with it he encloses the sacrifice, he, as it were, wraps it around with it. Therefore it is called upaveṣa.

children.text: tena prāco 'ṅgārānudūhati
children.translated_text: With it he draws the coals eastward.

children.text: apāgne agnimāmādaṃ jahi niṣkravyādaṃ sedhetyayaṃ vā āmādyenedam manuṣyāḥ paktvāśnantyatha yena puruṣaṃ dahanti sa kravyādetāvevaitadubhāvato 'pahanti ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Agni</s>, drive away the raw-eating fire; drive away the flesh-eating one." This is the raw-eater, the fire with which men cook and eat; and the one with which they burn a person is the flesh-eater. Thus he drives both of these away from here.

children.text: athāṅgāramāskauti
children.translated_text: Then he throws on a coal.

children.text: ā devayajaṃ vaheti yo devayāṭ tasmin havīṃṣi śrapayāma tasminyajñaṃ tanavāmahā iti tasmādvā āskauti ||
children.translated_text: "Bring it to the place of divine sacrifice." "On that fire which sacrifices to the gods let us cook the oblations; on that let us extend the sacrifice." Therefore he throws it on.

children.text: tam madhyamena kapālenābhyupadadhāti
children.translated_text: He covers it with the middle potsherd.

children.text: devā ha vai yajñaṃtanvānāste 'surarakṣasebhya āsaṅgādbibhayāṃcakrur nenno 'dhastānnāṣṭrā rakṣāṃsyupottiṣṭhānityagnirhi rakṣasāmapahantā tasmādevamupadadhāti tadyadeṣa eva bhavati nānya eṣa hi yajuṣkṛto medhyastasmānmadhyamena kapālenābhyupadadhāti ||
children.translated_text: The gods, when extending the sacrifice, feared danger from the asuras and rakṣases, thinking, "Let not the hostile rakṣases rise up against us from below." For <s>Agni</s> is the repeller of rakṣases; therefore he lays it down in this way. And because it is this very one and no other, this one is purified by the yajus and fit for sacrifice; therefore he covers it with the middle potsherd.

children.text: sa upadadhāti
children.translated_text: He lays it down.

children.text: dhruvamasi pṛthivīṃ dṛṃheti pṛthivyā eva rūpeṇaitadeva dṛṃhatyetenaiva dviṣantam bhrātṛvyamavabādhate brahmavani tvā kṣatravani sajātavanyupadadhāmi bhrātṛvyasya vadhāyeti bahvī vai yajuh svāśīstadbrahma ca kṣatraṃ cāśāsta ubhe vīrya sajātavanīti bhūmā vai sajātāstadbhūmānamāśāsta upadadhāmi bhrātṛvyasy ||
children.translated_text: "You are firm; make the earth firm." Thus, by means of the earth's own form, he makes this very thing firm. By this he drives away the hateful rival. "For winning <s>brahman</s>, for winning <s>kṣatra</s>, for winning those of the same birth, I lay you down for the slaying of the rival." The <s>yajus</s> is indeed manifold and rich in its own blessing. Thereby he has wished for both <s>brahman</s> and <s>kṣatra</s>, both forms of vigor. "For winning those of the same birth": multitude indeed is those of the same birth; thereby he has wished for multitude. "I lay you down for the rival's ..."

children.text: athāṅgāramāskauti
children.translated_text: Then he scatters an ember.

children.text: nediha purā nāṣṭrā rakṣāṃsyāviśāniti brāhmaṇo hi raksasāmapahantā tasmādabhinihitameva savyasya pāṇeraṅgulyā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: This is so that the <s>rakṣases</s> may not enter here before, through the evil power; for the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is the smiter of the <s>rakṣases</s>. Therefore an ember is held close with a finger of the left hand.

children.text: athāṅgāramadhyūhati
children.translated_text: Then he pushes an ember over it.

children.text: agne brahma gṛbhṇīṣveti nediha purā nāṣṭrā rakṣāṃsyāviśānityagnirhi rakṣasām apahantā tasmādenamadhyūhati ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Agni</s>, take hold of <s>brahman</s>," so that the <s>rakṣases</s> may not enter here before, through the evil power; for <s>Agni</s> is the smiter of the <s>rakṣases</s>. Therefore he pushes it over him.

children.text: atha yatpaścāttadupadadhāti
children.translated_text: Then he lays down the one that is at the back.

children.text: dharuṇamasyantarikṣaṃ dṛṃhetyantarikṣasyaiva rūpeṇaitadeva dṛṃhatyetenaiva dviṣantam bhrātṛvyamavabādhate brahmavani tvā kṣatravani sajātavanyupadadhāmi bhrātṛvyasya badhāyeti ||
children.translated_text: "You are the support; make the atmosphere firm." Thus, by means of the atmosphere's own form, he makes this very thing firm. By this he drives away the hateful rival. "For winning <s>brahman</s>, for winning <s>kṣatra</s>, for winning those of the same birth, I lay you down for the slaying of the rival."

children.text: atha yatpurastāttadupadadhāti
children.translated_text: Then he lays down the one that is in front.

children.text: dhartramasi divaṃ dṛṃheti diva eva rūpeṇaitadeva dṛṃhatyetenaiva ... badhaayeti ||
children.translated_text: "You are the supporter; make heaven firm." Thus, by means of heaven's own form, he makes this very thing firm. By this he ... for slaying.

children.text: atha yaddakṣiṇatastadupapadhāti
children.translated_text: Then he lays down the one that is on the south.

children.text: viśvābhyastvāśābhya upadadhāmīti sa yadimāṃllokānati caturthamasti vā na vā tenaivaitaddviṣantam bhrātṛvyamavabādhate 'naddhā vai tadyadimāṃllokānati caturthamasti vā na vānaddho tadyadviśvā āśāstasmādāha viśvābhyastvāśābhya upadadhāmīti tūṣṇīṃ vaivetarāṇi kapālānyupadadhāti cita ||
children.translated_text: "For all the quarters I lay you down." Now whatever fourth thing there is, or is not, beyond these worlds, by that very thing he drives away the hateful rival. Uncertain indeed is whatever fourth thing there is, or is not, beyond these worlds; uncertain is that which is all the quarters. Therefore he says, "For all the quarters I lay you down." But he lays down the other potsherds silently, piled up.

children.text: athāṅgārairabhyūhati
children.translated_text: Then he covers it over with embers.

children.text: bhṛgūṇāmaṅgirasāṃ tapasā tapyadhvamityetadvai tejiṣṭhaṃ tejo yadbhṛgvaṅgirasāM sutaptānyasanniti tasmādenamabhyūhati ||
children.translated_text: "Be heated with the heat of the <s>Bhṛgus</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s>." This indeed is the keenest heat, that of the <s>Bhṛgus</s> and <s>Aṅgirases</s>; he does it so that they may be well heated. Therefore he covers it over with them.

children.text: atha yo dṛṣadupale upadadhāti
children.translated_text: Then, when he lays down the grinding stone and the upper stone,

children.text: sa kṛṣṇājinamādatte śarmāsīti tadavadhūnotyavadhūtaṃ rakṣo 'vadhūtā arātaya iti so 'sāveva bandhustatpratīcīnagrīvamupastṛṇātyadityāstvagasi prati tvāditirvettviti so 'sāveva bandhuh ||
children.translated_text: he takes up the black antelope skin. "You are shelter." He shakes it out: "Shaken off is the <s>rakṣas</s>; shaken off are the enemies." That is the very same connection. He spreads it with its neck toward the west: "You are <s>Aditi</s>'s skin; may <s>Aditi</s> recognize you." That is the very same connection.

children.text: atha dṛṣadamupadadhāti
children.translated_text: Then he lays down the grinding stone.

children.text: dhiṣaṇāsi parvatī prati tvādityāstvagvettviti dhiṣaṇā hi parvatī hi prati tvādityāstvagvettviti tatsaṃjñāmevaitatkṛṣṇājināya ca vadati nedanyo 'nyaṃ hinasāva itīyamevaiṣā pṛthivī rūpeṇa ||
children.translated_text: "You are <s>Dhiṣaṇā</s>, mountain-born; may <s>Aditi</s>'s skin recognize you." For <s>Dhiṣaṇā</s> is indeed mountain-born. "May <s>Aditi</s>'s skin recognize you": thereby he speaks an agreement between the black antelope skin and it, so that one may not injure the other. This is the earth itself in form.

children.text: atha śamyāmudīcīnāgrāmupadadhāti
children.translated_text: Then he lays down the pin with its point to the north.

children.text: diva skambhanīrasītyantarikṣameva rūpeṇāntarikṣeṇa hīme dyāvāprthivī viṣṭabdhe tasmādāha diva skambhanīrasīti ||
children.translated_text: "You are the prop of heaven." It is the atmosphere itself in form, for by the atmosphere these two, heaven and earth, are propped apart. Therefore he says, "You are the prop of heaven."

children.text: athopalāmupadadhāti
children.translated_text: Then he lays down the upper stone.

children.text: dhiṣaṇāsi pārvateyī prati tvā parvatī vettviti kanīyasī hyeṣā duhiteva bhavati tasmād āha pārvateyīti prati tvā parvatī vettviti prati hi svaḥ saṃjānīte tatsaṃjñāmevaitaddṛṣadupalābhyāṃ vadati ned anyonyaṃ hinasāta iti dyaurevaiṣā rūpeṇa hanū eva dṛṣadupalejihvaiva śamyā tasmāchamyayā samāatha haviradhivapati
children.translated_text: "You are <s>Dhiṣaṇā</s>, daughter of the mountain; may the mountain-born one recognize you." For this one is smaller, like a daughter; therefore he says, "daughter of the mountain." "May the mountain-born one recognize you": for one's own kin recognizes one. Thereby he speaks an agreement between the grinding stone and the upper stone, so that they may not injure each other. This is heaven itself in form. The grinding stone and upper stone are the two jaws, and the pin is the tongue; therefore he unites them with the pin. Then he pours the oblation on.

children.text: dhānyamasi dhinuhi devāniti dhānyaṃ hi devāndhinavadityu hi havirgṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: "You are grain; satisfy the gods." For grain will satisfy the gods, since the oblation is taken up.

children.text: atha pinaṣṭi
children.translated_text: Then he grinds it.

children.text: prāṇāya tvodānāya tvā vyānāya tvā dīrghāmanu prasitimāyuṣe dhāmiti prohati devo vaḥ savitā hiraṇyapāṇiḥ pratigṛbhṇātvachidreṇa pāṇinā cakṣuṣe tveti ||
children.translated_text: "For the breath I take you; for the up-breath I take you; for the through-breath I take you; for long extension, for life, I place you." He pours it forth: "May the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, golden-handed, receive you with an uninjured hand. For sight I take you."

children.text: tadyadevam pinaṣṭi
children.translated_text: As to why he grinds it in this way:

children.text: jīvaṃ vai devānāṃ haviramṛtamamṛtānāmathaitadulūkhalamusalābhyāṃ dṛṣadupalābhyāṃ haviryajñaṃ ghnanti ||
children.translated_text: the oblation of the gods is living, immortal among the immortals; but with the mortar and pestle, with the grinding stone and upper stone, they strike the oblation, the sacrifice.

children.text: sa yadāha
children.translated_text: When he says,

children.text: prāṇāya tvodānāya tveti tatprāṇodānau dadhāti vyānāya tveti tadvyānaṃ dadhāti dīrghāmanu prasitimāyuṣe dhāmiti tadāyurdadhāti devo vaḥ savitā hiraṇyapāṇiḥ pratigṛbhṇātvachidreṇa pāṇinā supratigṛhītānyasanniti cakṣuṣe tveti taccakṣurdadhātyetāni vai jīvato bhavantyevamu haitajjīvameva devānāṃ havirbhavatyam athaika ājyaṃ nirvapati
children.translated_text: "For the breath I take you; for the up-breath I take you," he thereby places breath and up-breath in it. "For the through-breath I take you": thereby he places through-breath in it. "For long extension, for life, I place you": thereby he places life-span in it. "May the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, golden-handed, receive you with an uninjured hand," so that they may be well received. "For sight I take you": thereby he places sight in it. These belong to a living being; in this way this oblation of the gods becomes living. Then one pours out ghee.

children.text: yadvā ādiṣṭaṃ devatāyai havirgṛhyate yāvaddevatyaṃ tadbhavati taditareṇa yajuṣā gṛhṇāti na vā etatkasyai cana devatāyai havirgṛhṇannādiśati yadājyaṃ tasmādaniruktena yajuṣā gṛhṇāti mahīnām payo 'sīti mahya iti ha vā etāsāmeke nāma yadgavāṃ tāsāṃ vā etatpayo bhavati tasmādāha mahīnām payo 'sī ||
children.translated_text: When an oblation is taken with a deity specified, it belongs to just that deity. He takes the other one with a <s>yajus</s>. But when he takes ghee, he does not specify that he is taking the oblation for any deity. Therefore he takes it with an undefined <s>yajus</s>: "You are the milk of the great ones." Some say that "great ones" is a name for cows; this indeed is their milk. Therefore he says, "You are the milk of the great ones."

children.text: Chapter 4
caturdhā vihito ha vā agre 'gnirāsa
children.translated_text: In the beginning, <s>Agni</s> was divided fourfold.

children.text: sa yamagre 'gniṃ hotrāya prāvṛṇata sa prādhanvad yaṃ dvitīyam prāvṛṇata sa praivādhanvad yaṃ tṛtīyam prāvṛṇata sa praivādhanvad atha yo 'yametarhyagniṃ sa bhīṣā nililye so 'paḥ praviveśa taṃ devā anuvidya sahasaivādbhya āninyuḥ so 'po 'bhitiṣṭhevāvaṣṭhyūtā stha yā aprapadanaṃ stha yābhyo vo mām akāmaṃ nayantīti tata āptyāḥ saṃbabhūvustrito dvita ekataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whichever <s>Agni</s> they chose first for the hotṛ-priesthood ran away; whichever they chose second ran away too; whichever they chose third likewise ran away. But this <s>Agni</s> of the present, out of fear, hid himself and entered the waters. The gods, having discovered him, suddenly brought him forth from the waters. He stood upon the waters and said, 'You are spat upon; you are without footing, since you bring me unwillingly from among you.' From that arose the <s>Āptyas</s>: <s>Trita</s>, <s>Dvita</s>, and <s>Ekata</s>.

children.text: ta indreṇa saha ceruḥ
children.translated_text: They went about together with <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: yathedam brāhmaṇo rājānamanucarati sa yatra triśīrṣāṇaṃ tvāṣṭraṃ viśvarūpaṃ jaghāna tasya haite 'pi vadhyasya vidāṃcakruḥ śaśvaddhainaṃ trita eva jaghānāty aha tadindro 'mucyata devo hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as a brahmin here follows a king, so they followed him. When he slew the three-headed son of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, they too came to know of that slaying. Indeed <s>Trita</s> himself repeatedly struck him down, yet from that <s>Indra</s> was released, for he was a god.

children.text: ta u haita ūcuḥ
children.translated_text: Then they said:

children.text: upaivema eno gacchantu ye 'sya vadhyasyāvediṣuriti kimiti yajña evaiṣu mṛṣṭām iti tadeṣvetad yajño mṛṣṭe yad ebhyaḥ pātrīnirṇejanam aṅgulipraṇejanaṃ ninayanti ||
children.translated_text: 'Let those who knew of his slaying come near to this guilt.' 'In what way?' 'Let the sacrifice itself wipe it off among them.' Therefore the sacrifice wipes this off among them when people pour away for them the vessel-rinsing and the finger-rinsing water.

children.text: ta u hāptyā ūcuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Āptyas</s> said:

children.text: atyeva vayamidamasmatparo nayāmeti kamabhīti ya evādakṣiṇena haviṣā yajātā iti tasmānnādakṣiṇena haviṣā yajetāptyeṣu ha yajño mṛṣṭa āptyā u ha tasminmṛjate yo 'dakṣiṇena haviṣā yajate ||
children.translated_text: 'Let us carry this away beyond ourselves.' 'Against whom?' 'Against the one who sacrifices with an offering that has no dakṣiṇā (priestly fee).' Therefore one should not sacrifice with an offering without dakṣiṇā. Among the <s>Āptyas</s> the sacrifice has been wiped clean, and the <s>Āptyas</s> wipe themselves upon the man who sacrifices with an offering without dakṣiṇā.

children.text: tato devāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the gods

children.text: etām darśapūrṇamāsayor dakṣiṇām akalpan yadanvāhāryaṃ nedadakṣiṇaṃ havirasaditi tannānā ninayati tathaibhyo 'samadaṃ karoti tadabhitapati tathaiṣāṃ śṛtam bhavati sa ninayati tritāya tvā dvitāya tvaikatāya tveti paśurha vā eṣa ālabhyate yatpuroḍāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: devised this dakṣiṇā for the new- and full-moon sacrifices, namely the anvāhārya, so that the oblation might not be without dakṣiṇā. He pours it away separately; in that way he makes it free from mixture for them. He heats it; in that way it becomes cooked for them. He pours it away with, 'For <s>Trita</s> you, for <s>Dvita</s> you, for <s>Ekata</s> you.' For this, namely the sacrificial cake, is an animal being offered.

children.text: puruṣaṃ ha vai devāḥ
children.translated_text: For the gods

children.text: agre paśumālebhire tasyālabdhasya medho 'pacakrāma so 'śvaṃ praviveśa te 'śvamālabhanta tasyālabdhasya medho 'pacakrāma sa gām praviveśa te gām ālabhanta tasyālabdhasya medho 'pacakrāma so 'vim praviveśa te 'vim ālabhanta tasyālabdhasya medho 'pacakrāma so 'jam praviveśa te 'jamālabhanta tasyālabdhasya medho 'pacakrāma ||
children.translated_text: first offered a man as the sacrificial animal. When he had been offered, his sacrificial essence went away and entered the horse. They offered the horse; when it had been offered, its sacrificial essence went away and entered the cow. They offered the cow; when it had been offered, its sacrificial essence went away and entered the sheep. They offered the sheep; when it had been offered, its sacrificial essence went away and entered the goat. They offered the goat; when it had been offered, its sacrificial essence went away.

children.text: sa imām pṛthivīm praviveśa
children.translated_text: It entered this earth.

children.text: taṃ khananta ivānvīṣus tamanvavindaṃs tāvimau vrīhiyavau tasmādapyetāvetarhi khananta ivaivānuvindanti sa yāvadvīryavaddha vā asyaite sarve paśava ālabdhāḥ syus tāvadvīryavaddhāsya havireva bhavati ya evametad vedātro sā sampadyadāhuḥ pāṅktaḥ paśuriti ||
children.translated_text: They sought it as though digging, and they found it; these two, rice and barley, are what they found. Therefore even now people find these two just as if by digging. As much strength as all these sacrificial animals of his would have if offered, just so much strength his oblation has, who knows this. Here is fulfilled what they say: 'The animal is fivefold.'

children.text: yadā piṣṭānyatha lomāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: When the grains are ground, then they become the hairs.

children.text: yadāpa ānayatyatha tvagbhavati yadā saṃyautyatha māṃsam bhavati saṃtata iva hi sa tarhi bhavati saṃtatamiva hi māṃsaṃ yadā śṛto 'thāsthi bhavati dāruṇa iva hi sa tarhi bhavati dāruṇamityasthyatha yadudvāsayiṣyannabhighārayati tam majjānaṃ dadhāty eṣo sā sampadyadāhuḥ pāṅktaḥ paśuriti ||
children.translated_text: When he brings water, then it becomes the skin. When he kneads it together, then it becomes the flesh, for at that time it is, as it were, continuous, and flesh is as it were continuous. When it is cooked, then it becomes bone, for at that time it is hard, and bone is hard. And when, about to take it down, he sprinkles it with ghee, he places marrow in it. This is the fulfillment of what they say: 'The animal is fivefold.'

children.text: sa yam puruṣamālabhanta
children.translated_text: The man whom they offered

children.text: sa kimpuruṣo 'bhavad yāvaśvaṃ ca gāṃ ca tau gauraśca gavayaścābhavatāṃ yamavimālabhanta sa uṣṭro 'bhavad yamajamālabhanta sa śarabho 'bhavat tasmādeteṣām paśūnāṃ nāśitavyam apakrāntamedhā haite paśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: became a kimpuruṣa. The horse and the cow became a gaur and a gavaya. The sheep whom they offered became a camel. The goat whom they offered became a śarabha. Therefore these animals are not to be eaten; these animals have had their sacrificial essence departed from them.

children.text: Chapter 5
ādityena caruṇodayanīyena pracarati
children.translated_text: He proceeds with the Āditya caru, the concluding offering.

children.text: tadyadādityaścarurbhavati yadevaināmado devā abruvaṃs tavaiva prāyaṇīyas tavodayanīya iti tamevāsyā etadubhayatra bhāgaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: Now because it is an Āditya caru: when the gods said to her then, 'Yours alone is the opening offering; yours is the concluding offering,' he thereby assigns to her that portion in both places.

children.text: sa yadamutra rājānaṃ kreṣyannupapraiṣyan yajate
children.translated_text: When, intending to buy the king over there and to send him forth, he sacrifices,

children.text: tasmāttatprāyaṇīyaṃ nāmātha yadatrāvabhṛthādudetya yajate tasmādetadudayanīyaṃ nāma tadvā etatsamānameva havir adityā eva prāyaṇīyamadityā udayanīyam iyaṃ hyevāditiḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore that is called the prāyaṇīya. And when, after coming up here from the avabhṛtha bath, he sacrifices, therefore this is called the udayanīya. But this is in fact the very same oblation: the prāyaṇīya belongs to <s>Aditi</s>, and the udayanīya belongs to <s>Aditi</s>, for this earth is <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text: sa vai pathyāmevāgre svastiṃ yajati
children.translated_text: First he sacrifices to <s>Pathyā Svasti</s>.

children.text: taddevā aprajñāyamāne vācaiva pratyapadyanta vācā hi mugdham prajñāyate 'thātra prajñāte yathāpūrvaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: When it was not yet understood, the gods reached it through speech, for through speech something confused is understood. Then, when it has been understood, he performs as before.

children.text: so 'gnimeva prathamaṃ yajati
children.translated_text: He sacrifices first to <s>Agni</s>,

children.text: atha somamatha savitāramatha pathyāṃ svastimathāditiṃ vāgvai pathyā svastiriyamaditirasyāmeva taddevā vācam pratyaṣṭhāpayantseyaṃ vāgasyām pratiṣṭhitā vadati ||
children.translated_text: then to <s>Soma</s>, then to <s>Savitṛ</s>, then to <s>Pathyā Svasti</s>, and then to <s>Aditi</s>. Speech is <s>Pathyā Svasti</s>; this earth is <s>Aditi</s>. Thereby the gods established speech upon this earth, and this speech, established upon it, speaks.

children.text: atha maitrāvaruṇīṃ vaśāmanūbandhyāmālabhate
children.translated_text: Then he offers the barren cow for <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> as the anūbandhyā animal.

children.text: sa eṣo 'nya eva yajñastāyate paśubandha eva samiṣṭayajūṃṣi hyevānto yajñasya ||
children.translated_text: This is a distinct sacrifice that is extended, namely the animal sacrifice; for the samiṣṭayajus formulas are the end of the sacrifice.

children.text: tadyanmaitrāvaruṇī vaśā bhavati
children.translated_text: Now because it is a barren cow for <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>:

children.text: yadvā ījānasya sviṣṭam bhavati mitro 'sya tadgṛhṇāti yadvasya duriṣṭam bhavati varuṇo 'sya tadgṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: whatever of the sacrificer's rite is well sacrificed, <s>Mitra</s> takes that; whatever of his rite is badly sacrificed, <s>Varuṇa</s> takes that.

children.text: tadāhuḥ
children.translated_text: On this they say:

children.text: kve jāno 'bhūditi tadyadevāsyātra mitraḥ sviṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāti tadevāsmā etayā prītaḥ pratyavasṛjati yadu cāsya varuṇo duriṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāti taccaivāsmā etayā prītaḥ sviṣṭaṃ karoti tadu cāsmai pratyavasṛjati so 'syaiṣa sva eva yajño bhavati svaṃ sukṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'Where has the people gone?' On this point, whatever of his rite <s>Mitra</s> here takes as well sacrificed, that very thing, pleased by this offering, he releases back to him; and whatever of his rite <s>Varuṇa</s> takes as badly sacrificed, that too, pleased by this offering, he makes well sacrificed for him and releases back to him. Thus this sacrifice of his becomes his own, his own good deed.

children.text: tadyanmaitrāvaruṇī vaśā bhavati
children.translated_text: As to why it is a barren cow for <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>:

children.text: yatra vai devā retaḥ siktam prājanayaṃstadāgnimārutamityukthaṃ tasmiṃstadvyākhyāyate yathā taddevā retaḥ prājanayaṃstato 'ṅgārāḥ samabhavannaṅgārebhyo 'ṅgirasastadanvanye paśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where the gods generated the semen that had been poured out, that is explained in the chant called Āgnimāruta: just as the gods generated that semen, from it embers came into being; from the embers came the <s>Aṅgirases</s>; after that came the other animals.

children.text: atha yadāsāḥ pāṃsavaḥ paryaśiṣyanta
children.translated_text: Then, when those dusty remnants were left over,

children.text: tato gardabhaḥ samabhavattasmādyatra pāṃsulam bhavati gardabhasthānam iva batetyāhuratha yadā na kaścana rasaḥ paryaśiṣyata tata eṣā maitrāvaruṇī vaśā samabhavattasmādeṣā na prajāyate rasāddhi retaḥ sambhavati retasaḥ paśavastadyadantataḥ samabhavattasmādantaṃ yajñasyānuvartate ta ||
children.translated_text: from them the donkey came into being. Therefore, where a place is dusty, people say, 'Why, it is like a donkey's place.' Then, when no sap at all was left over, from that this barren cow for <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> came into being. Therefore she does not give birth, for semen comes from sap, and animals from semen. Because she came into being at the end, therefore she follows the end of the sacrifice.

children.text: athetaraṃ viśve devā amarīmṛtsyanta
children.translated_text: Then the other animals the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> handled among themselves.

children.text: tato vaiśvadevī samabhavadatha bārhaspatyā so 'nto 'nto hi bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: From that came the victim for the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s>; then the one for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. That one is the end, for <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the end.

children.text: sa yaḥ sahasraṃ vā bhūyo vā dadyāt
children.translated_text: Whoever should give a thousand or more,

children.text: sa enāḥ sarvā ālabheta sarvaṃ vai tasyāptam bhavati sarvaṃ jitaṃ yaḥ sahasraṃ vā bhūyo vā dadāti sarvametā evameva yathāpūrvam maitrāvaruṇīmevāgre 'tha vaiśvadevīmatha bārhaspatyam ||
children.translated_text: he should offer all these. For everything is obtained by him, everything is won, who gives a thousand or more. All these are offered just in this order as before: first the Maitrāvaruṇī, then the Vaiśvadevī, then the Bārhaspatya.

children.text: atho ye dīrghasattramāsīran
children.translated_text: And those who should sit through a long sattra,

children.text: saṃvatsaraṃ vā bhūyo vā ta enāḥ sarvā ālabherantsarvaṃ vai teṣāmāptam bhavati sarvaṃ jitaṃ ye dīrghasattramāsate saṃvatsaraṃ vā bhūyo vā sarvametā evameva yathāpūrvam ||
children.translated_text: for a year or more, should offer all these. For everything is obtained by them, everything is won, who sit through a long sattra for a year or more. All these are offered just in this order as before.

children.text: athodavasānīyayeṣṭyā yajate
children.translated_text: Then he sacrifices with the concluding iṣṭi.

children.text: sa āgneyam pañcakapālam puroḍāśaṃ nirvapati tasya pañcapadāḥ paṅktayo yājyānuvākyā bhavanti yātayāmeva vā etadījānasya yajño bhavati so 'smātparāṅiva bhavatyagnirvai sarve yajñā agnau hi sarvān yajñāṃs tanvate ye ca pākayajñā ye cetare tadyajñamevaitatpunarārabhate tathāsyāyātayāmā yajño ||
children.translated_text: He prepares for <s>Agni</s> a sacrificial cake on five potsherds. Its invitatory and offering verses are paṅkti-verses of five feet. For the sacrifice of one who has sacrificed has, as it were, become worn out; it becomes, as it were, turned away from him. <s>Agni</s> is all sacrifices, for in <s>Agni</s> they extend all sacrifices, both the domestic offerings and the others. Therefore by this he takes up the sacrifice again, and so his sacrifice is unworn.

children.text: tad yat pañcakapālaḥ puroḍāśo bhavati
children.translated_text: As to why the sacrificial cake is on five potsherds:

children.text: pañcapadāḥ paṅktayo yājyānuvākyāḥ pāṅkto vai yajñastadyajñam evaitat punarārabhate tathāsyāyātayāmā yajño bhavati tatho asmānna parāṅ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: the invitatory and offering verses are paṅkti-verses of five feet; the sacrifice is paṅkta, fivefold. Therefore by this he takes up the sacrifice again, and so his sacrifice becomes unworn, and so it does not turn away from him.

children.text: tasya hiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇā
children.translated_text: For it, gold is the dakṣiṇā (priestly fee).

children.text: āgneyo vā eṣa yajño bhavatyagne reto hiraṇyaṃ tasmāddhiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇānaḍvaanvā sa hi vahenāgneyo 'gnidagdhamiva hyasya vaham bhavati ||
children.translated_text: This sacrifice belongs to <s>Agni</s>, and gold is the seed of <s>Agni</s>; therefore gold is the dakṣiṇā. Or an ox, for it is a bearer and belongs to <s>Agni</s>, since his carrying-load is as if burned by fire.

children.text: atho caturgṛhītamevājyaṃ gṛhītvā
children.translated_text: Then, taking ghee in four ladlings,

children.text: vaiṣṇavyarcā juhotyuru viṣṇo vikramasvoru kṣayāya naskṛdhi ghṛtaṃ ghṛtayone piba pra pra yajñapatiṃ tira svāheti yajño vaiviṣṇustadyajñamevaitatpunarārabhate tathāsyāyātayāmā yajño bhavati tatho asmānna parāṅ bhavati tatro yachaknuyāttaddadyānnādakṣiṇaṃ haviḥ syāditi hyāhuratha y ||
children.translated_text: he offers with a verse to <s>Viṣṇu</s>: 'Stride widely, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>; make wide room for our dwelling. Drink the ghee, O ghee-born one. Carry the lord of sacrifice forward and across. Svāhā.' The sacrifice is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Therefore by this he takes up the sacrifice again, and so his sacrifice becomes unworn, and so it does not turn away from him. There he should give whatever he can, for people say, 'Let no oblation be without dakṣiṇā.' Then y...

children.text: Chapter 6
vaśāmālabhate
children.translated_text: he offers the barren cow.

children.text: tāmālabhya saṃjñapayanti saṃjñapyāha vapāmutkhidetyutkhidya vapāmanumarśaṃ garbham eṣṭavai brūyāt sa yadi na vindanti kimādriyeran yady u vindanti tatra prāyaścittiḥ kriyate ||
children.translated_text: Having offered her, they make her lie still. After making her lie still, he says, 'Cut out the omentum.' Having cut out the omentum, he should say, 'Search along for a fetus.' If they do not find one, why should they be concerned? But if they do find one, then an expiation is performed there.

children.text: na vai tadavakalpate
children.translated_text: That is not properly fitting,

children.text: yadekām manyamānā ekayevaitayā careyur yaddve manyamānā dvābhyāmiva careyu sthālīṃ caivoṣṇīṣaṃ copakalpayitavai brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: that, thinking it to be one, they would proceed with this one alone; or that, thinking there are two, they would proceed as if with two. He should tell them to prepare both a cooking pot and a turban-cloth.

children.text: atha vapayā caranti
children.translated_text: Then they proceed with the omentum.

children.text: yathaiva tasyai caraṇaṃ vapayā caritvādhvaryuśca yajamānaśca punaretaḥ sa āhādhvaryur nirūhaitaṃ garbhamiti taṃ ha nodarato nirūhedārtāyā vai mṛtāyā udarato nirūhanti yadā vai garbhaḥ samṛddho bhavati prajananena vai sa tarhi pratyaṅṅaiti tamapi virujya śroṇī pratyañcaṃ nirūhitavai brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: Just as the procedure for it is, after they have proceeded with the omentum, the adhvaryu and the sacrificer return. The adhvaryu says, 'Take out this fetus.' But he should not take it out from the belly, for they take a fetus from the belly of one that is afflicted or dead. When a fetus is fully developed, then it comes out backward through the birth passage. He should tell them to split apart the pelvis and take it out backward.

children.text: taṃ nirūhyamāṇam abhimantrayate
children.translated_text: As it is being taken out, he addresses it with a mantra:

children.text: ejatu daśamāsyo garbho jarāyuṇā saheti sa yadāhaijatviti prāṇam evāsminnetad dadhāti daśamāsya iti yadā vai garbhaḥ samṛddho bhavatyatha daśamāsyas tametadapy adaśamāsyaṃ santam brahmaṇaiva yajuṣā daśamāsyaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: 'Let the ten-month fetus stir together with the afterbirth.' When he says, 'Let it stir,' he thereby places breath in it. When he says, 'ten-month,' then, since when a fetus is fully developed it is ten-month, he makes it, although it is not ten-month, ten-month by the sacred formulation, by the <s>yajus</s>.

children.text: jarāyuṇā saheti
children.translated_text: 'Together with the afterbirth,'

children.text: tadyathā daśamāsyo jarāyuṇā saheyādevametadāha yathāyaṃ vāyurejati yathā samudra ejatīti prāṇamevāsminnetaddadhātyevāyaṃ daśamāsyo 'srajjarāyuṇā saheti tadyathā daśamāsyo jarāyuṇā saha sraṃsetaivametadāha ||
children.translated_text: for just as a ten-month fetus would move together with the afterbirth, so he says this. 'As this wind stirs, as the sea stirs': thereby he places breath in it. 'This ten-month one has slipped forth together with the afterbirth': just as a ten-month fetus would slip forth together with the afterbirth, so he says this.

children.text: tadāhuḥ
children.translated_text: On this they say:

children.text: kathametaṃ garbhaṃ kuryādity aṅgādaṅgāddhaivāsyāvadyeyur yathaivetareṣāmavadānānām avadānaṃ tad u tathā na kuryād uta hyeṣo 'vikṛtāṅgo bhavatyadhastādeva grīvā apikṛtyaitasyāṃ sthālyāmetam medhaṃ ścotayeyuḥ sarvebhyo vā asyaiṣo 'ṅgebhyo medha ścotati tadasya sarveṣāmevāṅgānāmavattam bhavatyavadyanti vaśāyā avadānāni yathaiva teṣāmavadānam ||
children.translated_text: How should one deal with this embryo? They would surely cut portions from its limb after limb, just as there is a portioning of the other portions. But one should not do so in that way, for this one has its limbs unaltered. Cutting off just below the neck, they should cause this fat to drip into this pot. This fat indeed drips from all her limbs; therefore for him it becomes taken from all the limbs. They cut the portions of the barren cow just as those portions are cut.

children.text: tāni paśuśrapaṇe śrapayanti
children.translated_text: They cook those in the animal-cooking vessel.

children.text: tadevaitam medhaṃ śrapayanty uṣṇīṣeṇāveṣṭya garbham pārśvataḥ paśuśrapaṇasyopanidadhāti yadā śṛto bhavatyatha samudyāvadānānyevābhijuhoti naitam medham udvāsayanti paśuṃ tadevaitam medhamudvāsayanti ||
children.translated_text: They cook this fat in the same way. Having wrapped the embryo in a turban cloth, he places it at the side of the animal-cooking vessel. When it is cooked, then he offers only the collected portions. They do not take this fat off the fire separately; by taking off the animal, they take off this fat.

children.text: taṃ jaghanena cātvālamantareṇa yūpaṃ cāgniṃ ca haranti
children.translated_text: They carry it behind the cātvāla pit, between the sacrificial post and the fire.

children.text: dakṣiṇato nidhāya pratiprasthātāvadyatyatha srucor upastṛṇīte 'tha manotāyai haviṣo 'nuvāca āhāvadyanti vaśāyā avadānānāṃ yathaiva teṣāmavadānam ||
children.translated_text: Having set it down on the south side, the <s>pratiprasthātṛ</s> cuts off portions. Then he spreads underlaying ghee in the two ladles. Then, when he has recited the invitatory formula for <s>Manotā</s>'s oblation, they cut portions of the barren cow's portions just as those portions are cut.

children.text: atha pracaraṇīti srugbhavati
children.translated_text: Then there is a ladle called the pracaraṇī.

children.text: tasyām pratiprasthātā medhāyopastṛṇīte dviravadyati sakṛdabhighārayati pratyanaktyavadāne athānuvāca āhāśrāvyāha preṣyeti vaṣaṭkṛte 'dhvaryurjuhoty adhvaryoranu homaṃ juhoti pratiprasthātā ||
children.translated_text: In it the <s>pratiprasthātṛ</s> spreads underlaying ghee for the fat, cuts off twice, pours ghee over once, and anoints the portions. Then, when he has recited, has had the call to attention made, and has said, "Proceed," at the vaṣaṭ-call the <s>adhvaryu</s> offers, and after the <s>adhvaryu</s>'s oblation the <s>pratiprasthātṛ</s> offers.

children.text: yasyai te yajñiyo garbha iti
children.translated_text: "For her whose embryo of yours is fit for sacrifice," he says.

children.text: ayajñiyā vai garbhās tametadbrahmaṇaiva yajuṣā yajñiyaṃ karoti yasyai yonir hiraṇyayītyado vā etasyai yoniṃ vicchindanti yadado niṣkarṣanty amṛtamāyurhiraṇyaṃ tāmevāsyā etadamṛtāṃ yoniṃ karoty aṅgānyahrutā yasya tam mātrā samajīgamaṃ svāheti yadi pumānt syād yady u strī syād aṅgānyahrutā yasyai tāṃ mātrā samajīgamaṃ svāheti yadyvavijñāto garbho bhavati puṃskṛtyaiva juhuyāt pumāṃso hi garbhā aṅgānyahrutā yasya taṃ mātrā samajīgamaṃ svāhety ado vā etaṃ mātrā viṣvañcaṃ kurvanti yad ado niṣkarṣanti tam etad brahmaṇaiva yajuṣā samardhya madhyato yajñasya punarmātrā saṃgamayati ||
children.translated_text: Embryos are indeed unfit for sacrifice; by this sacred utterance, by the <s>yajus</s>, he makes it fit for sacrifice. "For her whose womb is golden": for they sever this one's womb when they draw it out. Gold is immortal life; by this he makes an immortal womb for her. "Whose limbs are uninjured, him I have brought together with his mother. Svāhā," if it is male. But if it is female, he says, "Whose limbs are uninjured, her I have brought together with her mother. Svāhā." If the embryo is not recognized, he should offer making it masculine, for embryos are male: "Whose limbs are uninjured, him I have brought together with his mother. Svāhā." For they make this one separated from its mother when they draw it out. By this sacred utterance, by the <s>yajus</s>, having made it complete, he reunites it with its mother in the middle of the sacrifice.

children.text: athādhvaryur vanaspatinā carati
children.translated_text: Then the <s>adhvaryu</s> proceeds with the offering to <s>Vanaspati</s>.

children.text: vanaspatinādhvaryuścaritvā yānyupabhṛtyavadānāni bhavanti tāni samānayamāna āhāgnaye sviṣṭakṛte 'nubrūhīty atyākrāmati pratiprasthātā sa etaṃ sarvameva medhaṃ gṛhṇīte 'thopariṣṭād dvir ājyasyābhighārayaty āśrāvyāha preṣyeti vaṣaṭkṛte 'dhvaryurjuhoty adhvaryoranu homaṃ juhoti pratiprasthātā ||
children.translated_text: After the <s>adhvaryu</s> has proceeded with <s>Vanaspati</s>, while he is bringing together the portions that are in the upabhṛt ladle, he says, "Recite for <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>." The <s>pratiprasthātṛ</s> steps across. He takes all this fat. Then on top he pours ghee over it twice. Having had the call to attention made and having said, "Proceed," at the vaṣaṭ-call the <s>adhvaryu</s> offers, and after the <s>adhvaryu</s>'s oblation the <s>pratiprasthātṛ</s> offers.

children.text: purudasmo viṣurūpa induriti
children.translated_text: "Rich in wonders, of manifold form, the drop," he says.

children.text: bahudāna iti haitadyadāha purudasma iti viṣurūpa iti viṣurūpā iva hi garbhā indurantarmahimānamānañja dhīra ityantarhyeṣa mātaryakto bhavatyekapadīṃ dvipadīṃ tripadīṃ catuṣpadīmaṣṭāpadīmbhuvanānu prathantāṃ svāheti prathayatyevaināmetatsubhūyo ha jayatyaṣṭāpadyeṣṭvā yaducānaṣṭāpadyā ||
children.translated_text: When he says "rich in wonders," that means "giving much." "Of manifold form," for embryos are as it were of manifold form. "The drop, the wise one, has anointed its inner greatness," for this one is anointed within its mother. "May she, one-footed, two-footed, three-footed, four-footed, eight-footed, extend through the worlds. Svāhā." By this he makes her extend. He wins a still better thing by sacrificing with an eight-footed verse than with a verse that is not eight-footed.

children.text: tadāhuḥ
children.translated_text: On this they say:

children.text: kvaitaṃ garbhaṃ kuryāditi vr%kṣa evainamuddadhyurantarikṣāyatanā vai garbhā antarikṣamivaitadyadvr%kṣastadenaṃ sva evāyatane pratiṣṭhāpayati tadu vā āhurya enaṃ tatrānuvyāharedvr%kṣa enam mr%tamuddhāsyantīti tathā haiva syāt ||
children.translated_text: "Where should one place this embryo?" They should raise it onto a tree, for embryos have the atmosphere as their resting place, and a tree is, as it were, the atmosphere. Thus he establishes it in its own resting place. But they also say, "Whoever should speak against him there would say, 'They will raise him dead onto a tree.'" And that would indeed be so.

children.text: apa evainamabhyavahareyuḥ
children.translated_text: They should carry it down to the waters.

children.text: āpo vā asya sarvasya pratiṣṭhā tadenamapsveva pratiṣṭhāpayati tadu vā āhurya enaṃ tatrānuvyāharedapsveva mariṣyatīti tathā haiva syāt ||
children.translated_text: The waters are indeed the foundation of all this. Thus he establishes it in the waters. But they also say, "Whoever should speak against him there would say, 'He will die in the waters themselves.'" And that would indeed be so.

children.text: ākhūtkara evainamupakireyuḥ
children.translated_text: They should heap it over in a molehill.

children.text: iyaṃ vā asya sarvasya pratiṣṭhā tadenamasyāmeva pratiṣṭhāpayati tadu vā āhur ya enaṃ tatrānuvyāharetkṣipre 'smai mr%tāya śmaśānaṃ kariṣyantīti tathā haiva syāt ||
children.translated_text: This earth is indeed the foundation of all this. Thus he establishes it on this very earth. But they also say, "Whoever should speak against him there would say, 'They will quickly make a cremation-ground for him when he is dead.'" And that would indeed be so.

children.text: paśuśrapaṇa evainam marudbhyo juhuyāt
children.translated_text: He should offer it to the <s>Maruts</s> in the animal-cooking fire.

children.text: ahutādo vai devānām maruto viḍahutamivaitadyadaśr%to garbha āhavanīyād vā eṣa āhr%to bhavati paśuśrapaṇastathāha na bahirdhā yajñādbhavati na pratyakṣamivāhavanīye devānāṃ vai marutastadenam marutsveva pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Maruts</s> are indeed the eaters of what has not been offered among the gods. This is as though offered to the clans, since the embryo is uncooked. This animal-cooking fire has been brought from the āhavanīya fire; thus it is not outside the sacrifice, nor is it visibly in the āhavanīya. The <s>Maruts</s> belong to the gods; therefore he establishes it among the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: sa hutvaiva samiṣṭayajūṃṣi
children.translated_text: Having offered and after the samiṣṭayajus formulas,

children.text: prathamāvaśānteṣvaṅgāreṣvetaṃ soṣṇīṣaṃ garbhamādatte taṃ prāṅ tiṣṭhañjuhoti mārutyarcā maruto yasya hi kṣaye pāthā divo vimahasaḥ sa sugopātamo jana iti na svāhākarotyahutādo vai devānām maruto viḍahutamivaitadyadasvāhākr%taṃ devānāṃ vai marutastadenam marutsveva pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: when the first embers have subsided, he takes up this embryo together with the turban cloth. Standing facing east, he offers it with a verse to the <s>Maruts</s>: "O <s>Maruts</s>, in whose abode the paths of heaven are of vast greatness, that man is best protected." He does not pronounce svāhā. The <s>Maruts</s> are indeed the eaters of what has not been offered among the gods. This is as though offered to the clans, since it is not made with svāhā. The <s>Maruts</s> belong to the gods; therefore he establishes it among the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: athāṅgārairabhisamūhati
children.translated_text: Then he rakes embers together over it.

children.text: mahī dyauḥ pr%thivī ca na imaṃ yajñam mimikṣatām pipr%tāṃ no bharīmabhiriti ||
children.translated_text: "May great heaven and earth mix this sacrifice for us; may they fill us with nourishments," he says.

children.text: Chapter 7
taṃ vai mādhyaṃdine savane 'bhiṣiñcati
children.translated_text: He consecrates him at the midday pressing.

children.text: eṣa vai prajāpatirya eṣa yajñastāyate yasmādimāḥ prajāḥ prajātā etamevāpyetarhyanu prajāyante tadenam madhyata evaitasya prajāpaterdadhāti madhyataḥ suvati ||
children.translated_text: This sacrifice that is being spread out is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>; from him these creatures were born, and even now they are born after him. Thus he places him in the very middle of this <s>Prajāpati</s>; from the middle he impels him.

children.text: agṛhīte māhendre
children.translated_text: When the Māhendra cup has not yet been taken,

children.text: eṣa vā indrasya niṣkevalyo graho yanmāhendro 'pyasyaitanniṣkevalyameva stotraṃ niṣkevalyaṃ śastramindro vai yajamānastadenaṃ sva evāyatane 'bhiṣiñcati tasmādagṛhīte māhendre ||
children.translated_text: for this Māhendra cup is <s>Indra</s>'s own special cup; and this, too, is his own special chant and his own special recitation. <s>Indra</s> is the sacrificer. Thus he consecrates him in his own proper seat. Therefore it is when the Māhendra cup has not yet been taken.

children.text: agreṇa maitrāvaruṇasya dhiṣṇyam
children.translated_text: In front of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>'s hearth-seat,

children.text: śārdūlacarmopastṛṇāti somasya tviṣirasīti yatra vai soma indramatyapavata sa yattataḥ śārdūlaḥ samabhavattena somasya tviṣistasmādāha somasya tviṣirasīti taveva me tviṣirbhūyāditi śārdūlatviṣimevāsminnetaddadhāti tasmādāha taveva me tviṣirbhūyāditi ||
children.translated_text: he spreads out a tiger skin, saying, "You are the splendor of <s>Soma</s>." Where <s>Soma</s> flowed past <s>Indra</s>, from that the tiger came into being; by that it is the splendor of <s>Soma</s>. Therefore he says, "You are the splendor of <s>Soma</s>." "May your splendor become mine," he says. Thus he places tiger-splendor in him. Therefore he says, "May your splendor become mine."

children.text: atha pārthāni juhoti
children.translated_text: Then he offers the Pārtha oblations.

children.text: pṛthī ha vai vainyo manuṣyāṇām prathamo 'bhiṣiṣice so 'kāmayata sarvamannādyamavarundhīyeti tasmā etānyajuhavuḥ sa idaṃ sarvamannādyam avarurudhe 'pi ha smāsmā āraṇyānpaśūn abhihvayantyasāvehi rājā tvā pakṣyata iti tathedaṃ sarvamannādyamavarurudhe sarvaṃ ha vā annādyamavarunddhe yasyaivaṃ viduṣa etāni hvayante ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pṛthi Vainya</s> was the first of men to be consecrated. He desired, "May I secure all food and nourishment." For him they offered these oblations. He secured all this food and nourishment. Indeed even forest animals used to call out to him, "Come here, that king will cook you." In that way he secured all this food and nourishment. One for whom these oblations are called, knowing this, secures all food and nourishment.

children.text: tāni vai dvādaśa bhavanti
children.translated_text: They are twelve in number.

children.text: dvādaśa vai māsāḥ saṃvatsarasya tasmāddvādaśa bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: There are twelve months of the year; therefore they are twelve.

children.text: ṣaṭ purastādabhiṣekasya juhoti
children.translated_text: He offers six before the consecration

children.text: ṣaḍupariṣṭāttadenam madhyata evaitasya prajāpaterdadhāti madhyataḥ suvati ||
children.translated_text: and six afterward. Thus he places him in the very middle of this <s>Prajāpati</s>; from the middle he impels him.

children.text: sa yāni purastādabhiṣekasya juhoti
children.translated_text: Of those which he offers before the consecration,

children.text: bṛhaspatisteṣāmuttamo bhavatyatha yānyupariṣṭādabhiṣekasya juhotīndrasteṣām prathamo bhavati brahma vai bṛhaspatirindriyaṃ vīryamindra etābhyāmevainam etad vīryābhyāmubhayataḥ paribṛṃhati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the last; and of those which he offers after the consecration, <s>Indra</s> is the first. <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is brahman; <s>Indra</s> is power and heroic strength. With these two powers he strengthens him on both sides.

children.text: sa juhoti
children.translated_text: He offers:

children.text: yāni purastādabhiṣekasya juhotyagnaye svāheti tejo vā agnistejasaivainametadabhiṣiñcati somāya svāheti kṣatraṃ vai somaḥ kṣatreṇaivainametadabhiṣiñcati savitre svāheti savitā vai devānām prasavitā savitṛprasūta evainametadabhiṣiñcati sarasvatyai svāheti vāgvai sarasvatī vācaivainametadabhiṣiñcati pūṣṇe svāheti paśavo vai pūṣā paśubhirevainametadabhiṣiñcati bṛhaspataye svāheti brahma vai bṛhaspatir brahmaṇaivainam etad abhiṣiñcaty etāni purastādabhiṣekasya juhoti tānyetānyagnināmānyācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: the ones he offers before the consecration are: "To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā." <s>Agni</s> is brilliance; with brilliance he thereby consecrates him. "To <s>Soma</s>, svāhā." <s>Soma</s> is royal power; with royal power he thereby consecrates him. "To <s>Savitṛ</s>, svāhā." <s>Savitṛ</s> is the impeller of the gods; impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, he thereby consecrates him. "To <s>Sarasvatī</s>, svāhā." <s>Sarasvatī</s> is speech; with speech he thereby consecrates him. "To <s>Pūṣan</s>, svāhā." <s>Pūṣan</s> is cattle; with cattle he thereby consecrates him. "To <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, svāhā." <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is brahman; with brahman he thereby consecrates him. These he offers before the consecration; these they call the Agni-names.

children.text: atha juhoti
children.translated_text: Then he offers:

children.text: yānyupariṣṭādabhiṣekasya juhotīndrāya svāheti vīryaṃ vā indro vīryeṇaivainametadabhiṣiñcati ghoṣāya svāheti vīryaṃ vai ghoṣo vīryeṇaivainametadabhiṣiñcati ślokāya svāheti vīryaṃ vai śloko vīryeṇaivainametadabhiṣiñcatyaṃśāya svāheti vīryaṃ vā aṃśo vīryeṇaivainametadabhiṣiñcati bhagāya svāheti vīryaṃ vai bhago vīryeṇaivainametad abhiṣiñcaty aryamṇe svāheti tadenamasya sarvasyāryamaṇaṃ karotyetānyupariṣṭād abhiṣekasya juhoti tānyetāny ādityanāmānyācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: the ones he offers after the consecration are: "To <s>Indra</s>, svāhā." <s>Indra</s> is heroic strength; with heroic strength he thereby consecrates him. "To <s>Ghoṣa</s>, svāhā." <s>Ghoṣa</s> is heroic strength; with heroic strength he thereby consecrates him. "To <s>Śloka</s>, svāhā." <s>Śloka</s> is heroic strength; with heroic strength he thereby consecrates him. "To <s>Aṃśa</s>, svāhā." <s>Aṃśa</s> is heroic strength; with heroic strength he thereby consecrates him. "To <s>Bhaga</s>, svāhā." <s>Bhaga</s> is heroic strength; with heroic strength he thereby consecrates him. "To <s>Aryaman</s>, svāhā." Thereby he makes him the <s>Aryaman</s>, the lordly kinsman, of all this. These he offers after the consecration; these they call the Āditya-names.

children.text: agreṇa maitrāvaruṇasya dhiṣṇyam
children.translated_text: In front of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>'s hearth-seat,

children.text: abhiṣecanīyāni pātrāṇi bhavanti yatraitā āpo 'bhiṣecanīyā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: there are the consecration vessels, where these waters for consecration are.

children.text: pālāśam bhavati
children.translated_text: One is made of palāśa wood.

children.text: tena brāhmaṇo 'bhiṣiñcati brahma vai palāśo brahmaṇaivainametadabhiṣiñcati ||
children.translated_text: With it a brahmin consecrates him. The palāśa is brahman; with brahman he thereby consecrates him.

children.text: audumbaram bhavati
children.translated_text: One is made of udumbara wood.

children.text: tena svo 'bhiṣiñcatyannaṃ vā ūrg udumbara ūrgvai svaṃ yāvadvai puruṣasya svam bhavati naiva tāvadaśanāyati tenork svaṃ tasmādaudumbareṇa svo 'bhiṣiñcati ||
children.translated_text: With it his own people consecrate him. The udumbara is food, nourishment; one's own people are nourishment. As long as a man has his own people, just so long he does not hunger. Therefore his own people consecrate him with an udumbara vessel.

children.text: naiyagrodhapādam bhavati
children.translated_text: One is a foot of nyagrodha wood.

children.text: tena mitryo rājanyo 'bhiṣiñcati padbhirvai nyagrodhaḥ pratiṣṭhito mitreṇa vai rājanyaḥ pratiṣṭhitastasmānnaiyagrodhapādena mitryo rājanyo 'bhiṣiñcati ||
children.translated_text: With it a friendly kṣatriya consecrates him. The nyagrodha is established by its feet; a kṣatriya is established by alliance. Therefore a friendly kṣatriya consecrates him with a foot of nyagrodha wood.

children.text: āśvattham bhavati
children.translated_text: One is made of aśvattha wood.
