children.text: tena vaiśyo 'bhiṣiñcati sa yadevādo 'śvatthe tiṣṭhata indro maruta upāmantrayata tasmādāśvatthena vaiśyo 'bhiṣiñcatyetānyabhiṣecanīyāni pātrāṇi bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: With it a vaiśya consecrates him. Because <s>Indra</s>, standing there at the aśvattha, summoned the <s>Maruts</s>, therefore a vaiśya consecrates him with an aśvattha vessel. These are the consecration vessels.

children.text: atha pavitre karoti
children.translated_text: Then he prepares the two strainers.

children.text: pavitre stho vaiṣṇavyāviti so 'sāveva bandhustayorhiraṇyam pravayati tābhyāmetā abhiṣecanīyā apa utpunāti tadyaddhiraṇyam pravayatyamṛtamāyurhiraṇyaṃ tadāsvamṛtamāyurdadhāti tasmāddhiraṇyam pravayati ||
children.translated_text: "You two are strainers belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s>," he says; that is their very connection. He threads gold through them. With them he purifies these consecration waters. When he threads gold through, gold is immortality and life; thereby he places immortality and life in them. Therefore he threads gold through.

children.text: sa utpunāti
children.translated_text: He purifies them.

children.text: saviturvaḥ prasava utpunāmyachidreṇa pavitreṇa sūryasya raśmibhiriti so 'sāveva bandhur anibhṛṣṭamasi vāco bandhustapojā ityanādhṛṣṭā stha rakṣobhirityevaitadāha yad āhānibhṛṣṭamasīti vāco bandhuriti yāvadvai prāṇeṣv āpo bhavanti tāvadvācā vadati tasmādāha vāco bandhuriti ||
children.translated_text: "By the impulse of <s>Savitṛ</s> I purify you with an unbroken purifier, with the rays of the sun." That is the very same connection. "You are unassailed; you are the bond of speech; born of heat": in saying, "You are unassailed," he means, "You are unassailed by <s>rakṣases</s>." "The bond of speech": as long as there are waters in the breaths, so long one speaks with speech. Therefore he says, "the bond of speech."

children.text: tapojā iti
children.translated_text: "Born of heat."

children.text: agnirvai dhūmo jāyate dhūmādabhramabhrādvṛṣṭiragnervā etā jāyante tasmādāha tapojā iti ||
children.translated_text: For from fire smoke is born, from smoke cloud, and from cloud rain. These are born from fire; therefore he says, "born of heat."

children.text: somasya dātramasīti
children.translated_text: "You are <s>Soma</s>'s giver."

children.text: yadā vā enametābhirabhiṣuṇvantyathāhutirbhavati tasmādāha somasya dātramasīti svāhā rājasva iti tadenāḥ svāhākāreṇaivotpunāti ||
children.translated_text: When they press him with these waters, then he becomes an oblation. Therefore he says, "You are <s>Soma</s>'s giver." "Svāhā, be kingly": with the svāhā-call itself he purifies them upward.

children.text: tā eteṣu pātreṣu vyānayati
children.translated_text: He then distributes these among the vessels.

children.text: sadhamādo dyumninīr āpa etā ity anatimāninya ityevaitadāha yadāha sadhamāda iti dyumninīr āpa etā iti vīryavatya ityevaitadāhānādhṛṣṭā apasyo vasānā ityanādhṛṣṭā stha rakṣobhirityevaitadāha yadāhānādhṛṣṭā apasyo vasānā iti pastyāsu cakre varuṇaḥ sadhasthamiti viśo vai pastyā vikṣu cakre varuṇaḥ pratiṣṭhām ityevaitad āhāpāṃ śiśur mātṛtamāsvantar ityapāṃ vā eṣa śiśur bhavati yo rājasūyena yajate tasmād āhāpāṃ śiśur mātṛtamāsvantar iti ||
children.translated_text: "These waters are companions in exhilaration, brilliant." In saying "companions in exhilaration," he means just this: "not despising." "These waters are brilliant": he means just this, "possessed of vigor." "Unassailed, clothed in work": in saying "unassailed, clothed in work," he means just this, "you are unassailed by <s>rakṣases</s>." "<s>Varuṇa</s> made his common seat among the households": the households are the clans; he means just this, "<s>Varuṇa</s> made a foundation among the clans." "The child of the waters, within the most motherly ones": the man who sacrifices with the <s>Rājasūya</s> becomes a child of the waters. Therefore he says, "the child of the waters, within the most motherly ones."

children.text: athainaṃ vāsāṃsi paridhāpayati
children.translated_text: Then he causes him to put on garments.

children.text: tat tārpyamiti vāso bhavati tasmint sarvāṇi yajñarūpāṇi niṣyūtāni bhavanti tadenam paridhāpayati kṣatrasyolbamasīti tadyadeva kṣatrasyolbaṃ tata evainametajjanayati ||
children.translated_text: That is a garment of tārpya cloth; all the forms of the sacrifice are sewn into it. He makes him put it on with, "You are the caul of kṣatra." Whatever is the caul of kṣatra, from that very thing he here causes him to be born.

children.text: athainam pāṇḍvam paridhāpayati
children.translated_text: Then he causes him to put on the pāṇḍva garment.

children.text: kṣatrasya jarāyvasīti tadyadeva kṣatrasya jarāyu tata evainametajjanayati ||
children.translated_text: "You are the afterbirth of kṣatra." Whatever is the afterbirth of kṣatra, from that very thing he here causes him to be born.

children.text: athādhīvāsam pratimuñcati
children.translated_text: Then he fastens the outer covering on him.

children.text: kṣatrasya yonirasīti tadyaiva kṣatrasya yonistasyā evainametajjanayati ||
children.translated_text: "You are the womb of kṣatra." From that very womb of kṣatra he here causes him to be born.

children.text: athoṣṇīṣaṃ saṃhṛtya
children.translated_text: Then, having gathered up the turban,

children.text: purastādavagūhati kṣatrasya nābhirasīti tadyaiva kṣatrasya nābhistāmevāsminnetaddadhāti ||
children.translated_text: he covers him in front with it: "You are the navel of kṣatra." Whatever is the navel of kṣatra, that very thing he places in him here.

children.text: taddhaike
children.translated_text: Now some, indeed,

children.text: samantam pariveṣṭayanti nābhirvā asyaiṣā samantaṃ vā iyaṃ nābhiḥ paryetīti vadantastad u tathā na kuryāt purastād evāvagūhet purastāddhīyaṃ nābhistadyadenaṃ vāsāṃsi paridhāpayati janayatyevainametajjātamabhiṣiñcānīti tasmādenaṃ vāsāṃsi paridhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: wrap it all the way around, saying, "This is its navel, and this navel goes around all of it." But one should not do it that way. He should cover him only in front, for this navel is in front. Thus, when he causes him to put on the garments, he causes him to be born; "I shall consecrate him when he has been born." Therefore he causes him to put on garments.

children.text: taddhaike
children.translated_text: Now some, indeed,

children.text: nidadhatyetāni vāsāṃsyathainam punardīkṣitavasanam paridhāpayanti tad u tathā na kuryād aṅgāni vā asya janūrvāsāṃsyaṅgairhainaṃ sajanvā tanvā vyardhayanti varuṇyaṃ dīkṣitavasanaṃ sa eteṣāmevaikaṃ vāsasām paridadhīta tadenamaṅgairjanvā tanvā samardhayati varuṇyaṃ dīkṣitavasanaṃ tadenaṃ varuṇyād dīkṣitavasanāt pramuñcati ||
children.translated_text: put these garments aside and then cause him again to put on the consecrated person's garment. But one should not do it that way. For the garments are his limbs and his birth; they would separate him from his limbs, his birth, and his body. The consecrated person's garment belongs to <s>Varuṇa</s>. He should put on one of these very garments. Thereby he completes him with limbs, birth, and body, and releases him from the Varuṇa-bound garment of the consecrated person.

children.text: sa yatrāvabhṛthamabhyavaiti
children.translated_text: When he goes down to the avabhṛtha bath,

children.text: tadetadabhyavaharanti tatsaloma kriyate sa eteṣāmevaikaṃ vāsasām paridhāyodaiti tāni vaśāyai vā vapāyāṃ hutāyāṃ dadyādudavasānīyāyāṃ veṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: they bring these garments down there; that is done together with the hair. Wearing one of these very garments, he comes up. He should give those garments either when the omentum of the barren cow has been offered, or at the concluding iṣṭi.

children.text: atha dhanuradhitanoti
children.translated_text: Then he strings the bow.

children.text: indrasya vārtraghnamasīti vārtraghnaṃ vai dhanur indro vai yajamāno dvayena vā eṣa indro bhavati yacca kṣatriyo yad u ca yajamānastasmādāhendrasya vārtraghnamasīti ||
children.translated_text: "You are <s>Indra</s>'s slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>." The bow is indeed vārtraghna, a slayer of Vṛtra. <s>Indra</s> is the sacrificer; this man becomes <s>Indra</s> in two ways, both because he is a kṣatriya and because he is the sacrificer. Therefore he says, "You are <s>Indra</s>'s slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>."

children.text: atha bāhū vimārṣṭi
children.translated_text: Then he rubs the two arms.

children.text: mitrasyāsi varuṇasyāsīti bāhvorvai dhanur bāhubhyāṃ vai rājanyo maitrāvaruṇas tasmādāha mitrasyāsi varuṇasyāsīti tadasmai prayacchati tvayāyaṃ vṛtram badhediti tvayāyaṃ dviṣantam bhrātṛvyam badhed ityevaitadāha ||
children.translated_text: "You belong to <s>Mitra</s>; you belong to <s>Varuṇa</s>." The bow is for the two arms, and by the two arms the royal man is connected with <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>. Therefore he says, "You belong to <s>Mitra</s>; you belong to <s>Varuṇa</s>." He hands it to him: "With you may this man strike down <s>Vṛtra</s>." He means just this: "With you may this man strike down the hateful rival."

children.text: athāsmai tisra iṣūḥ prayacchati
children.translated_text: Then he hands him three arrows.

children.text: sa yayā prathamayā samarpaṇena parābhinatti saikā seyam pṛthivī saiṣā dṛbā nāmātha yayā viddhaḥ śayitvā jīvati vā mriyate vā sā dvitīyā tadidamantarikṣaṃ saiṣā rujā nāmātha yayāpaiva rādhnoti sā tṛtīyā sāsau dyauḥ saiṣā kṣumā nāmaitā hi vai tisra iṣavas tasmādasmai tisra iṣūḥ prayacchati
children.translated_text: The one with which, at the first fastening-on, he pierces through is one; this earth is that one, and it is named <s>Dṛbā</s>. The one by which, when struck, a man lies down and either lives or dies is the second; this atmosphere is that one, and it is named <s>Rujā</s>. The one by which he misses the mark is the third; that heaven is that one, and it is named <s>Kṣumā</s>. These indeed are the three arrows; therefore he hands him three arrows.

children.text: tāḥ prayacchati pātainam prāñcam pātainam pratyañcam pātainaṃ tiryañcaṃ digbhyaḥ pāteti tadasmai sarvā eva diśo 'śaravyāḥ karoti tadyadasmai dhanuḥ prayacchati vīryaṃ vā etadrājanyasya yaddhanur vīryavantamabhiṣiñcānīti tasmādvā asmā āyudham prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: He hands them over with, "Protect him in front; protect him from behind; protect him across; protect him from the quarters." Thereby he makes all the quarters free from arrows for him. Thus, when he gives him the bow, it is vigor for the royal man, for the bow is vigor; "I shall consecrate him as vigorous." Therefore he gives him a weapon.

children.text: athainamāvido vācayati
children.translated_text: Then he makes the proclamations be recited for him.

children.text: āvirmaryā ityaniruktam prajāpatirvā aniruktas tadenam prajāpataya āvedayati so 'smai savamanumanyate tenānumataḥ sūyate ||
children.translated_text: "Manifest, O worthy ones": this is undefined. <s>Prajāpati</s> is undefined; thereby he announces him to <s>Prajāpati</s>. <s>Prajāpati</s> grants him consent for the consecration, and, consented to by him, he is consecrated.

children.text: āvitto agnirgṛhapatiriti
children.translated_text: "Manifestly announced is <s>Agni</s>, the house-lord."

children.text: brahma agnistadenam brahmaṇa āvedayati tadasmai savamanumanyate tenānumataḥ sūyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is <s>Agni</s>; thereby he announces him to the <s>brahman</s>. It gives consent to his pressing; with its consent he is consecrated.

children.text: āvitto indro vṛddhaśravā iti
children.translated_text: "Announced is <s>Indra</s>, of growing fame," he says.

children.text: kṣatraṃ vā indrastadenaṃ kṣatrāyāvedayati tadasmai savamanumanyate tenānumataḥ sūyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> is royal power; thereby he announces him to royal power. It gives consent to his pressing; with its consent he is consecrated.

children.text: āvittau mitrāvaruṇau dhṛtavratāviti
children.translated_text: "Announced are <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, firm in vows," he says.

children.text: prāṇodānau vai mitrāvaruṇau tadenam prāṇodānābhyāmāvedayati tāvasmai savamanumanyete tābhyāmanumataḥ sūyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> are breath and upward breath; thereby he announces him to breath and upward breath. They give consent to his pressing; with their consent he is consecrated.

children.text: āvittaḥ pūṣā viśvavedā iti
children.translated_text: "Announced is <s>Pūṣan</s>, knowing all," he says.

children.text: paśavo vai pūṣā tadenam paśubhya āvedayati te 'smai savamanumanyante tairanumataḥ sū ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pūṣan</s> is the cattle; thereby he announces him to the cattle. They give consent to his pressing; with their consent he is consecrated.

children.text: āvitte dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśambhuvāviti
children.translated_text: "Announced are Heaven and Earth, bringing welfare to all," he says.

children.text: tadenamābhyāṃ dyāvāpṛthivībhyāmāvedayati te asmai savamanumanyete tābhyāmanumataḥ sūyate ||
children.translated_text: Thereby he announces him to these two, Heaven and Earth. They give consent to his pressing; with their consent he is consecrated.

children.text: āvittāditiruruśarmeti
children.translated_text: "Announced is <s>Aditi</s>, of broad shelter," he says.

children.text: iyaṃ vai pṛthivyaditistadenamasmai pṛthivyā āvedayati sāsmai savamanumanyate tayānumataḥ sūyate tadyābhya evainametaddevatābhya āvedayati tā asmai savamanumanyante tābhiranumataḥ sūyate ||
children.translated_text: This earth is <s>Aditi</s>; thereby he announces him to this earth. She gives consent to his pressing; with her consent he is consecrated. Thus, to whatever deities he announces him, they give consent to his pressing; with their consent he is consecrated.

children.text: Chapter 8
sa vai prayujāṃ havirbhiryajate
children.translated_text: He sacrifices with the oblations of the teams.

children.text: tadyatprayujāṃ havirbhiryajata ṛtūnvā etat suṣuvāṇo yuṅkte ta enamṛtavo yuktā vahanty ṛtūnvā prayuktānanucarati tasmātprayujāṃ havirbhiryajate ||
children.translated_text: As to why he sacrifices with the oblations of the teams: when he has undergone the soma-pressing, he thereby yokes the seasons. The seasons, yoked, carry him; he follows the seasons that have been set to work. Therefore he sacrifices with the oblations of the teams.

children.text: tāni vai dvādaśa bhavanti
children.translated_text: They are twelve in number.

children.text: dvādaśa vai māsāḥ saṃvatsarasya tasmāddvādaśa bhavanti māsi māsi yajetetyāhuḥ ko veda manuṣyasya tasmānna māsi māsi yajeta śamyāparāvyādhe śamyāparāvyādha eva ṣaḍbhiryajate prāṅ yān atha punarāvṛttaḥ śamyāparāvyādhe śamyāparāvyādha eva ṣaḍbhiryajate ||
children.translated_text: There are twelve months of the year; therefore there are twelve. They say, "He should sacrifice month by month." Who knows the fate of a human being? Therefore he should not sacrifice month by month. At the distance of a peg-cast, precisely at the distance of a peg-cast, he sacrifices with six while going eastward; then, having turned back, at the distance of a peg-cast, precisely at the distance of a peg-cast, he sacrifices with six.

children.text: tad u tathā na kuryāt
children.translated_text: But he should not do it in that way.

children.text: ṣaḍevaitāni pūrvāṇi havīṃṣi nirvapati samānabarhīṃṣi tāsāṃ devatānāṃ rūpaṃ yathā śiśire yuktvā prāñca ā prāvṛṣaṃ yāyus tatṣaḍṛtūn yuṅkte ta enaṃ ṣaḍṛtavo yuktāḥ prāñca ā prāvṛṣaṃ vahanti ṣaḍvartūnprayuktānāprāvṛṣamanucarati pūrvāgnivāhāṃ dvau dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: He offers just these six earlier oblations, with the same sacrificial grass, according to the form of those deities. Just as, having yoked in winter, they might go eastward up to the rainy season, so he yokes the six seasons. Those six seasons, yoked, carry him eastward up to the rainy season; he follows the six seasons, set to work, up to the rainy season. The two oxen that draw the fore-fire are the dakṣiṇā.

children.text: ṣaḍevottarāṇi havīṃṣi nirvapati
children.translated_text: He offers just the six later oblations.

children.text: samānabarhīṃṣi tāsāṃ devatānāṃ rūpaṃ yathā punarāvarteranvārṣikamabhi tatṣaḍṛtūnyuṅkte ta enaṃ ṣaḍṛtavo yuktā vārṣikamabhi vahanti ṣaḍvartūnprayuktānvārṣikamanucarati pūrvāgnivāhāṃ dvau dakṣiṇā tad yat pūrvāgnivāho dakṣiṇartūn vā etatsuṣuvāṇo yuṅkte vahanti vā anaḍvāhas tasmāt pūrvāgnivāho dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: They have the same sacrificial grass, according to the form of those deities. Just as they would turn back again toward the yearly round, so he yokes the six seasons. Those six seasons, yoked, carry him toward the yearly round; he follows the six seasons, set to work, toward the yearly round. The two oxen that draw the fore-fire are the dakṣiṇā. As to why the dakṣiṇā consists of oxen that draw the fore-fire: when he has undergone the soma-pressing, he thereby yokes the seasons, and oxen do carry; therefore the dakṣiṇā consists of oxen that draw the fore-fire.

children.text: taddha smaitatpurā kurupañcālā āhuḥ
children.translated_text: Formerly the <s>Kuru-Pañcālas</s> used to say this:

children.text: ṛtavo vā asmānyuktā vahanty ṛtūnvā prayuktānanucarāma iti yadeṣāṃ rājāno rājasūyayājina āsustaddha sma tadabhyāhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: "The seasons, yoked, carry us; we follow the seasons that have been set to work." Since their kings were performers of the <s>rājasūya</s>, they used to say this about it.

children.text: āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ puroḍāśo bhavati
children.translated_text: There is an eight-cup sacrificial cake for <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: saumyaścaruḥ sāvitro dvādaśakapālo vāṣṭākapālo vā puroḍāśo bārhaspatyaś carustvāṣṭro daśakapālaḥ puroḍāśo vaiśvānaro dvādaśakapāla etāni ṣaṭ pūrvāṇi havīṃṣi bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: There is a caru for <s>Soma</s>; a twelve-cup or eight-cup sacrificial cake for <s>Savitṛ</s>; a caru for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; a ten-cup sacrificial cake for <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>; and a twelve-cup cake for <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. These are the six earlier oblations.

children.text: ṣaḍevottare caravaḥ
children.translated_text: The six later ones are carus.

children.text: sārasvataścaruḥ pauṣṇaścarur maitraścaruḥ kṣaitrapatyaścarur vāruṇaścarur ādityaścarur eta u ṣaḍuttare caravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A caru for <s>Sarasvatī</s>, a caru for <s>Pūṣan</s>, a caru for <s>Mitra</s>, a caru for the Lord of the Field, a caru for <s>Varuṇa</s>, and a caru for <s>Āditya</s>: these, then, are the six later carus.

children.text: atha śyenīṃ vicitragarbhāmadityā ālabhate
children.translated_text: Then he lays hold of a speckled-wombed she-falcon for <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text: tasyā eṣaivāvṛd yāṣṭāpadyai vaśāyā iyaṃ vā aditir asyā evainametadgarbhaṃ karoti tasyā etādṛśyeva śyenī vicitragarbhā dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: Her procedure is just the same as that for the eight-footed barren cow. This earth is <s>Aditi</s>; thereby he makes him an embryo of this very earth. For her the dakṣiṇā is a she-falcon of just that kind, speckled in the womb.

children.text: atha pṛṣatīṃ vicitragarbhām marudbhya ālabhate
children.translated_text: Then he lays hold of a speckled-wombed dappled cow for the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: tasyā eṣaivāvṛd viśo vai maruto viśāmevainametadgarbhaṃ karoti tasyāṃ etādṛśyeva pṛṣatī vicitragarbhā dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: Her procedure is just the same. The <s>Maruts</s> are the clans; thereby he makes him an embryo of the clans. For her the dakṣiṇā is a dappled cow of just that kind, speckled in the womb.

children.text: etau paśubandhau
children.translated_text: These are the two animal sacrifices.

children.text: tadetāveva santāvanyathevālabhante yāmadityā ālabhanta ādityebhyastāmālabhante sarvaṃ vā ādityāḥ sarvasyaivainametadgarbhaṃ karoti yām marudbhya ālabhante viśvebhyastāṃ devebhya ālabhante sarvaṃ vai viśve devāḥ sarvasyaivainametadgarbhaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: Yet while these two remain the same, they lay hold of them as if differently: the one they lay hold of for <s>Aditi</s>, they lay hold of for the <s>Ādityas</s>; for the <s>Ādityas</s> are everything, and thereby he makes him an embryo of everything. The one they lay hold of for the <s>Maruts</s>, they lay hold of for all the gods; for all the gods are everything, and thereby he makes him an embryo of everything.

children.text: Chapter 9
vibhūrmātrā prabhūḥ pitreti
children.translated_text: "Wide in measure, mighty as father," he says.

children.text: iyaṃ vai mātāsau pitābhyāmevainam paridadāty aśvo'si hayo'sīti śāstyevainaṃ tattasmācchiṣṭāḥ prajā jāyante 'tyo'si mayo'sīty atyevainaṃ nayati tasmādaśvaḥ paśūnāṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ gacchaty arvāsi saptirasi vājyasīti yathāyajurevaitad vṛṣāsi nṛmaṇā asīti mithunatvāya yayur nāmāsi śiśurnāmāsīty etad vā aśvasya priyaṃ nāmadheyaṃ priyeṇaivainaṃ nāmnābhivadati tasmād apyāmitrau saṃgatya nāmnā ced abhivadato 'nyonyaṃ sam eva jānāte ||
children.translated_text: This earth is the mother, that world is the father; with these two he surrounds him. "You are a horse; you are a steed," he recites: thereby he instructs him, and therefore instructed offspring are born. "You are a runner; you are delight," he leads him onward by that very means; therefore the horse attains preeminence among animals. "You are swift; you are a racer; you are strong for the prize": this is just according to the <s>yajus</s>. "You are a bull; you are man-minded": this is for pairing. "Your name is Yayu; your name is Child": this is the horse's dear name. By his dear name he addresses him; therefore even enemies, on meeting, if they address one another by name, come to recognize one another.

children.text: ādityānām patvānvihīti
children.translated_text: "Go along the path of the <s>Ādityas</s>," he says.

children.text: ādityānevainaṃ gamayati devā āśāpālā etaṃ devebhyo'śvam medhāya prokṣitaṃ rakṣateti śataṃ vai talpyā rājaputrā āśāpālās tebhya evainam paridadātīha rantiriha ramatāmiha dhṛtiriha svadhṛtiḥ svāheti saṃvatsaramāhutīrjuhoti ṣoḍaśa navatīr etā vā aśvasya bandhanaṃ tābhirevainam badhnāti tasmādaśvaḥ pramukto bandhanam āgacchati ṣoḍaśa navatīr etā vā aśvasya bandhanaṃ tābhir evainaṃ badhnāti tasmād aśvaḥ pramukto bandhanaṃ na jahāti ||
children.translated_text: He thereby makes him go to the <s>Ādityas</s>. "O gods, guardians of the quarters, protect this horse, consecrated for <s>medha</s> (sacrifice), for the gods." A hundred couch-born princes are indeed guardians of the quarters; to them he hands him over. "Here may pleasure be, here may he delight, here may firmness be, here may self-firmness be. Svāhā." For a year he offers oblations, sixteen nineties of them. These are the horse's bonds; with them he binds him. Therefore a horse, when released, comes back to its bond. Sixteen nineties of them: these are indeed the horse's bonds; with these very ones he binds him. Therefore a horse, when released, does not abandon its bond.

children.text: rāṣṭraṃ vā aśvamedhaḥ rāṣṭra ete vyāyacchante ye'śvaṃ rakṣanti teṣāṃ ya udṛcaṃ gacchanti rāṣṭreṇaiva te rāṣṭram bhavanty atha ye nodṛcaṃ gacchanti rāṣṭrātte vyavacchidyante tasmādrāṣṭryaśvamedhena yajeta parā vā eṣa sicyate yo'balo'śvamedhena yajate yadyamitrā aśvaṃ vinderan yajño'sya vicchidyeta pāpīyāntsyāc chataṃ kavacino rakṣanti yajñasya saṃtatyā avyavacchedāya na pāpīyān bhavaty athānyam ānīya prokṣeyuḥ saiva tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Aśvamedha</s> is the kingdom. Those who guard the horse contend over the kingdom. Those among them who reach the final verse become a kingdom through the kingdom itself; but those who do not reach the final verse are cut off from the kingdom. Therefore a royal man should sacrifice with the <s>Aśvamedha</s>. He who is weak and sacrifices with the <s>Aśvamedha</s> is poured away, as it were. If enemies should find the horse, his sacrifice would be interrupted and he would become worse off. A hundred men in armor guard it for the continuity of the sacrifice and so that it may not be interrupted; he does not become worse off. Then they should bring another and consecrate it. That is the expiation in that case.
